Inside that gap the device is busy rather than hung: `DIAG,win_gap` **206** rows (one every 13.8 ms), `PERS` 89, `DIAG,snapshot_unit` 79, `DIAG,stop_grain` 35, `DIAG,lcr` 28, `DIAG,win_readiness` **13** (`owes_currency, window_rebuild`, ~200 ms cadence), `LED` 147, `MI,U` 37 — while `MO` (MIDI out) is **0** and `DISP`/`DFRAME` fall to 2 rows each; at the resume `DIAG,playback_build,snapshot,1448,0,1536,…` completes and `DIAG,late_route,144,8,0,0,54,0` records **max 0 µs** for the notes that did leave, i.e. the lateness is upstream of the MIDI route. **Discriminators:** the *second* overdub has no gap at all (first row +6 ms, zero `win_readiness`), and `…-t8s4-01` ran on the **previous commit** with the same signature — so this is not the run-end transport-gesture change, which `…-t8s4-05` re-confirms (`run_end_transport_stop=host_realtime_stop`, `transport_press_count=1`, record `1536/1536` `raw 1536`, `record_grid_first_note_tick=0`, shutdown `complete/2/ok`, no latch). **Folded into the same record (same class, different observation):** after an interrupted run left the board playing, an 8 s read-only attach found the firmware alive (`[Memory] ext` once per second, queries answered) with **zero** `DFRAME`/`DISP`/`#CAP` rows — a dark screen — restored immediately by the managed run's soft `!REBOOT` (no upload, no flash). **Lead, not a root cause:** the window supply of a sounding slot that is simultaneously carrying the previous take's finalization/persistence (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild` currency/build path; `LoopContentResolution`'s `lcr,srcskip,…reason=not_finished` at the gap start), with the confirmation path named in the packet. **2026-10-05 — `windowed-playback-generation`: the windowed leg drives a slot switch; the gesture is proven safe on
hardware, and the missing demand is traced into the launch path's silent exits -- not to the root and not to the lane (host
tooling + authorized device runs; no firmware change).**
`run_windowed_content_parity` gained a **switch leg** (select a filled non-active target, press record, wait, then drain),
off by default and gated on a running transport. The safety argument is a code fact: with the track playing and the target
filled, `MidiButtonActions`' recording branch is unreachable (`slotCanArmForRecord = !hasCommittedPassesInSlot(slot)`) so
only a playback switch can queue -- and the device confirmed it with `Loop 4: Queued playback switch`, never
`Start Recording`, followed by the switch being **held and named** (`slot_switch_hold_exceeded track=7 target=3 age=3072
ticks`). The lane nonetheless stayed `eligible=progress=0` in all 85 `win_gap` blocks (66 with `running=1`), and the same
capture explains it: the target's on-demand restore was queued and never completed in the run (`RRQ,7,3,…queued`;
`capture_prewarm … ready=0`; no restore terminal), so a **cold target** gave neither the legacy merge nor the lane's launch
anything to prepare. Two host defects of mine were found by driving it (my flag reached the leg's strict parser and aborted
the first attempt; the port-lookup lesson recurred) and are now pinned, with M1 (order reversed) and M2 (gate removed)
red-proving the new pins and the file restored byte-identically. A second device attempt aborted at its own precondition
and is recorded as a setup failure, not evidence. **Run 04 revised the cause:** with a fresh qualification flash the target's restore **completed**
(`RRQ,7,3,...terminal,none,committed`) and the switch still held, with **no preparation activity at all** between the queue
and the hold — the leading cause (recorded as a **hypothesis** with its evidence) is the **LOOP_EDIT session** that the slot
selection itself opens immediately before the queue, since the lane refuses while an edit session is active and the S4b
device legs prepared their switches without one. Two runs made without a reboot aborted at the leg's own `clear failed`
precondition and are recorded as setup failures, not evidence. A trap is recorded with them: the reset must flash the
**qualification** image, because `hitl_boot_census.py` — the documented reset-by-re-upload path — hard-codes the **default**
env, where the lane is compiled off. **Run 05 refuted that too:** the driver now exits the edit session first (a long press on the edit control past the
firmware's 350 ms window, pinned; M3 red-proves the order), the device confirms `Long press - exited edit mode`, and the
queued switch **still** emitted no row of any kind for its whole bound — no `RRQ`, no `capture_prewarm`, no provision, no
launch, and no lane work (59 `win_gap`, all `eligible=progress=0`). **Run 06 + the code gate:** `servicePendingSlotProvision` asks the lane **only** for an `immutableLaunch` target
(not the active slot, and `shouldAvoidFullVisualRebuild(loopLength)` = **> 16 bars**), and the decisive input is the target's
**runtime** length — run 01's selection feedback read **`length=0`** for the 2-bar slot, putting that switch on the legacy
branch where no work happened at all, which explains runs 01/04/05. Run 06 (24-bar target) behaved identically and printed
no loop-length row, so the one value still missing is the long target's runtime length at switch time. The next step is
that measurement; the live question is no
longer about the leg: the next investigation is the **code** (`servicePendingSlotProvision` and its gating, no device
needed), with the S4b legs — whose switches did prepare and commit on this board — as the comparison. **Next, precisely:** warm the target first (play it, then switch away and
back) or let the queued restore complete, then re-run. Not claimed: the lane was not given work; F-7/F-8/AC-8 unverified;
6.4/6.5 open.

**The measurement was taken (2026-10-05) and its first classification is retracted; the trace that replaced it is committed (`evidence/2026-10-05-launch-path-trace/`).** What the rows show: the target is lane **slot 4** (the operator's "Loop 5"), a **24-bar** demoted slot, and the device reports its length itself at switch time (`Sent loop length CC feedback: 24 bars (18432 ticks) -> CC=23`), so the immutable-launch branch is taken; `provisionSlotForSwitch` did **not** refuse (zero `#MEM_DENIED` in all four switch runs); and the target's boot publication **completed and committed** (`RRQ,7,4,…terminal,none,committed`), after which the target produced **no row of any family**. The lane is not the constraint: in the *same* run it built six 2-bar `snapshot` windows (`windowLengthTicks 1536`, `eventCount 96`, one per bar) for the other 24-bar slot (index 5). So the first failed transition is inside `Track::preparePlaybackLaunchForSlot`, whose every exit is **silent** — `:2151-2152` (source request guard/failure), `:2167` (`prewarmRollingViews`), `:2168`/`:2174-2185`, `:2188` (role/pending) — and the existing rows cannot say which. Leading state, not a finding: an edit session rebuilt the active slot through the whole episode (3031 `note_edit` rows), the condition `:2188`'s `coverageRoleAvailable()` is sensitive to. Also corrected: `win_gap`'s `eligible/progress` counters read 0 **while the lane serves**, so they are not a work indicator. **Next:** a no-firmware driver variation (switch with the edit session provably closed); a narrow row at those exits only if that fails to discriminate.

**2026-10-05 — `windowed-playback-generation` 6.5 (native half): the two interleaving forces the suite did not force are
now forced on the playing chain (test-only slice; no production line edited, no device action).**
Slice 6.5 asks for the ten interleavings forced natively on the real request→worker→publication→consumption path, and
separately for the hardware half. The packet
([`EXECUTION.md`](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-05-s65-native-verification-split/EXECUTION.md))
inventoried the ten: two were **gaps**, and both are implemented.
`test_rolling_path_reuses_the_view_slot_after_a_refused_completion` forces **A→B→A view-slot reuse with the first A
completion arriving last**: A's build begins under its own operation identity and its completion is delivered after
ownership moved (the reader bumps the playback generation inside the final grain), so it publishes nothing (no ready
candidate, served view untouched, 0 events), the episode ends Idle, and the stale identity is *retained* — the refusal is
the guard, not a clean-up. B then takes the **same view slot** (which still carried A's identity), builds under the
**current** identity, and is **served**: 1536 serving ticks, 22 events = 11 note-ons + 11 closures, no foreign note.
`test_rolling_path_cancellation_between_every_preparation_grain_recovers` cancels at **every** preparation grain (k = 0..5,
at least one before the build began and at least one inside it) and asserts the same recovered state each time (frame Idle,
no pending/frozen demand, no builder, no candidate, served view untouched, 0 events, coverage source retired), then serves
one clean episode — the slot is **reusable**, not merely free. **Recorded rather than smoothed:** the explicit off-clock
cancellation after a late completion is a **no-op by measurement** (the completion already ended the episode, so
idempotence is what the fixture pins); the operation identity is stamped on **more than one path**, so mutation **MR-A**
(the build begin's stamp) is a **non-red-proof** while **MR-B** red-proves the ordering claim and **MR-C1/MR-C2** red-prove
the cancellation sweep, each restored byte-identically; and a fixture that forces a begin and then rewinds the clock kills
the episode (the drive must stay monotone). **Open by construction:** the interval A/B **revision trace** stays partial
(shared-view fixtures; no rolling-chain trace) and the whole **hardware** half is **NOT RUN** — it needs **6.4**'s
registered profile plus an authorized upload. Verification: focused **142/142**, full native **2796 / 2789 succeeded / 7
skipped / 0 failed**, capture build SUCCESS with the RAM1 line byte-identical, strict validation and `git diff --check`
clean. Evidence:
[`EVIDENCE.md`](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-05-s65-native-verification-split/EVIDENCE.md).
**Next:** 6.4 (registered device profile, host-only), then 6.5's hardware half under a dedicated HITL preset, after
authorization.

`job.ownsRawRange` without returning the sealed extent or re-arming the descriptor. Fixed (release one grain +
`reserveTail()`, plus the bounded idle safety net `Track::serviceCaptureStopDescriptorReservations()` with
`descriptor_rearm,ready|deny` and a skip for the two healthy states), native fixture red-proved,
`test_shared_capture_finalization` **60/60**, native trio 185/185, build + upload green with the RAM1 line unchanged.
On device: three consecutive `DROVE_LEG` on one boot (`s45-c4-…-180740-od1b`/`-180856-od2`/`-180957-od3`), stops
`finalize,…,deferred`, zero `descriptor_rearm` in the steady state. Then the campaign: pass 1
`s45-fixcamp-20261002-181057-od1` sealed `ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_PASS`; the next attempt was refused by the boot link
because the anchor's clock was a maximum over every row (its drained prefix holds the previous boot's tail,
194 649 907 us, while its own boot ended at 104 510 708 us) and the attempt side read a drained `#DMA_XFER` first
stamp. Fixed host-side (`current_boot_last_clock_us`, `cap_row_clock_us`, anchor close clock + close wall time,
`CLOCK_WALL_TOLERANCE_US = 10 s`), red-proved, restored byte-identically; the refused attempt re-grades to
`fresh_boot: ok` (64 919 717 us of device advance against 65 348 073 us of wall time), which exonerates the
interleaved parity read. Two real non-pass reasons remain on that attempt, both gate questions: a **serialized
successor** (**DEC-111 — a serialized acceptance run is NOT_EXERCISED**; the released interval held 0 events) and a
**resolved Hide** in slot 4 (effective 61 vs storage 63, the overdub's `(1225,On,71)` covering the record's
`(1238,On,71)`) where the guide scopes its count invariant to "this procedure's material" and the probe compares raw
`storage == effective`. **DEC-112 (owner ruling) now decides that and it is implemented:** the deduction is validated
as a **positive pass** (`hitl.content_deduction`, every difference named, an unexplained remainder still failing) —
the live device re-read reads `pass: true` with `slot 4: record#0 note 71 (On 1238, Off 1250) hidden by overdub#0 On
1225`, and that attempt's re-grade reads `content_parity: ok` beside the boot link `ok`, leaving the serialized
successor (DEC-111) as its only non-pass reason; the same entry rules the reproducer must be **clock/response-driven**
rather than raw-MIDI-timed. That ruling was implemented and then **measured** (`captures/s45-flow-20261002-191802-od1`):
the predecessor's window row is ring-buffered — it reached the file after the switch's directly printed row and only
once the 1.194 s window had closed — so no press can be placed on it; the flow keeps its immediate post-switch press,

**device-shaped** (192 ms window, 0-event release, against ~600 ms of the device's own admission latency). S4.5 open:
the **device investigation of that short, 0-event predecessor window**, three consecutive od passes, the record
leg's campaign (1 of 3) and S4f.11's cold-root undo/redo route. Verification: accepted-sequence **187/187**,

**The short-window anomaly is root-caused and reproduced.** The mid-interval loop-end wrap
(`src/Track/TrackOverdubWrap.cpp:145-147`) resets the capture staging and reseeds `captureGeneration` from a
`playbackGeneration` of **0**, so a leg that crosses its loop end arms a 0-generation release marker with an empty
staging: nothing owed → a ~200 ms window → the successor's ~600 ms admission lands after it
(`captures/s45-clock-20261002-194915-od1`, reproduced; healthy runs never wrap inside the leg). The host change here —

at **192 ticks per beat**, so the paced seed *was* its intended two bars (1536 ticks = 4.0 s) and the wrap is a
**phase** effect — a leg needs ~6 beats (4 of burst + the host's measured ~2-beat overhead) while the room at its
start tick was 8.5 beats in the healthy runs against 4.5 in the two that wrapped. `_run_plan` now sizes the burst from
the device's own numbers (loop length from its `RECS,stopToStopped` row, the leg's `@ tick` phase from its start row,

Options (2) then (1) were both taken. **(2) Native two-cycle fixture:** `test_second_record_cycle_is_admitted_with_every_guard_precondition_pinned`
drives record → stop → retire → clear → record → stop through the production stop path and pins every ownership

allocated, live Record capture, no owner) — **59/59**: the two-cycle pipeline is sound in isolation, so the device's
refusal has to come from state the harness cannot express. **(1) Named refusal on the board:** the admission now names
each of its refusals (`RECS,stage,deny_reason,<name>`, +64 B flash, **no** RAM1 cost — one file-scope slot, because a
`Track` member trips the S3.0 eight-way size assertion). Fresh boot, upload, pass 1 `DROVE_LEG`, then the repeat:
`RECS,stage,deny_reason,…,raw_range_unsealable` followed by `accepted_wait` — so the refusal is **not** the finalizer
owner, the canonical output, the job ring, the held notes, the slot/interval identity, the loop pool, the capture
phase or the state transition, but `loop.capture.store.canSealCaptureRange(job.rawRange)`. That check requires the
job's destination to be a **prepared empty successor directory** (one chunk, `Recording` lifecycle, refcount 1, full
pool capacity, unused) with a used tail on the producer — i.e. the second cycle's start did not leave the

preserve (its fallback is a plain `capture.store.clear()`). The pending save and the `transport_active` drain gate
seen earlier are **consequences** of the still-live take, not the cause. Campaign: 1 of 3 od passes on the restarted

**2026-10-02 — the campaign's repeat blocker is reproducible on a fresh boot and now code-localized.**
Following the authorized reboot, the first pass is a clean fresh-boot `ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_PASS`
(`captures/s45-campaign3-20261002-172937-od1`: both-slot content parity, timing clean, teardown complete, L1–L7 +
`overdub_interval_identity` + measured window green, sealed bundle), and the **second** attempt on that same boot
(`captures/s45-campaign3-20261002-173113-od2`) failed in exactly the same place as the earlier repeat — so the stall
is not an idle-time effect but the **second preparation of a boot**: the clear saves (`LoopPersist,slot:7:0,…,done`),
the transport starts, the take records (`RECA,4,0`), the host's commit stop lands (`Transport stopped` 105.996 s) and
the stop is **denied admission** — `RECS,stage,finalize,…,accepted_wait` is emitted only on
`Track::stopRecording`'s denial path (`TrackCaptureStopCommit.cpp`), where the stop is latched per DEC-067 and the
interval keeps recording (`DISP,4,RECORDING,1856,…`), while `PERS,request,0,135168,135168,already_pending` shows a
135 KB bundle still owed and **no** `PERS,drain` slice runs at all. The two guards a second cycle can newly trip are
the ones naming a resource the previous cycle still holds — `runtime->captureStopOwner != nullptr` or
`!runtime->canonicalCaptureOutputAdmitted()` (`TrackOverdubLifecycle.cpp`) — and the drain gate
`classifySyncDrainVerdict` refuses while a capture is live, so the take stays live because the stop was denied and
the drain is refused because the take is live: a circular wait between the record-stop admission and the persistence
drain, which unproven beyond the guard set. No firmware change made; the campaign is blocked at 1 of 3 od passes and
the next step is either a named denial reason at the admission or the native two-cycle reproducer.

**2026-10-02 — Phase 3: the campaign's repeat attempts are blocked by an accepted stop that never executed.**
Campaign rule: one boot, three consecutive passes, no reboot per attempt — so the oracle gained
`--boot-anchor <capture-or-run-dir>`, a checkable link to the boot a repeat continues (anchor banner, same image, no
restart row here, device clock continuing past the anchor's last stamp modulo the 32-bit `micros()`, with a capture
that leads with drained rows conservatively refused). `BootAnchorTests` **11/11** pin each part; reverting the link
red-proves the class. Pass 1 (fresh boot) stays sealed. **Attempt 2** (same boot, device clock 2570.5 s): clear, arm
and record are confirmed, the commit stop is **accepted** (`RECS,stage,record_stop,…,entered` then
`RECS,stage,finalize,…,accepted_wait`), and then nothing executes — the slot keeps recording
(`DISP,4,RECORDING,1912,…`) and the host ends `PREPARATION_FAILED`. **Attempt 3** cannot prepare: a save is owed and
its drain refuses while the transport reads active (`PERS,drain,transport_active,…`), so the scoped clear is refused
and the run ends `SHUTDOWN_INCOMPLETE_TIMEOUT`. The device state survives the attempt and its shutdown, so the
campaign is blocked at 1 of 3 with the count reset; clearing it needs a recovery reset that the plan forbids the
harness from doing automatically. Decision owed: recover and re-attempt, or investigate the un-retired accepted stop
as its own S4.5 blocker (owners: the record stop's deferred finalization, the persistence drain's `transport_active`
gate).
[Evidence](../../openspec/changes/runtime-working-set-ownership/evidence/2026-10-02-s45-preparation/FIX.md).

**2026-10-01 — REGRESSION FIXED AND DEVICE-VERIFIED: a 24-bar take crashed the device and then crash-looped it at every boot; the snapshot change set no longer allocates from the internal heap, and the restored library — the 24-bar body included — now boots.** Found while resolving S1.5: the take faulted at its **overdub wrap commit** (`captures/s15-24bar-01`: `Overdubbing wrap committed @ tick 18432` → reconnect → `boot_reset,crash=1`), after which the persisted body made every boot fault (~14 s cycles with the USB CDC dropping each time, each cycle's last activity `RRQ,4,0,…running` = **track 5 Loop 1**, exactly where the take was recorded). **Decoded:** `CrashReport` = **DACCVIOL, accessed address `0xB000`**, code at `0x600928B6` ⇒ `std::vector<SnapshotEventChange>::_M_realloc_insert`, `0xB000` = 45,056 = 512 × 88 = a vector with 512 elements and a **null `data()`**; the body-load path builds exactly that vector (`StorageLoopIoBodyFormatV1.cpp`, one `changes.events.push_back` per gathered event). **Why:** Teensyduino's `operator new` is `return malloc(size);` with no null check, while `std::vector` growth assumes a throwing allocator — a failed `malloc` on the fragmented internal heap (a ~45–180 KB request) hands the vector NULL and the growth copies into it (the first 32 KB of unmapped writes corrupt ITCM; `0xB000` is the first unmapped address). This one mechanism explains all three recorded `_M_realloc_insert` faults. **Fix (`cce0739a`):** `LoopSnapshotChangeSet` allocates its vectors through **`ExternalMemoryFirstAllocator`** (PSRAM-first; a **named FATAL** if both pools are exhausted), the body-load path **reserves** both vectors up front from the gather's known counts, and two **`static_assert`s** pin the types — reverting them **fails the build** (red-proofed, file restored byte-identically). **Device verification, all three approved steps (image `eca0b0139d864734ae5a3164126c20e18cbde60eb2c6b437df851126f988fc5a`):** flashed successfully (RAM1 guard `padding 1,336`, floor 840 met); a clean boot (`boot_reset,crash=0`, **no `CrashReport`**, one boot in 75 s, 71.9 s continuous uptime); `!RESTORE_WORKSPACE 5202` returned the library (`current.bad.5202 → current`, `checkpoints.bad.5202 → checkpoints`, four flags = 1); and on **two consecutive boots** the 24-bar body on track 5 Loop 1 **loads and reads back current** — `LIBOBS,S,t=4,s=0,…,l=18432,v=1152,kp=1,kr=1,kc=1` — with the library admitted (`post_restore_census … admission_complete=1 interactive_ready=1 undo_hydrated=1 transport_stopped=1`) and the observation complete over 64/64 slots with `restarts=0`. The block on large-content device acceptance is lifted; S4f.14 resumes. Evidence: [`evidence/2026-10-01-boot-crash-loop-24bar-take/FINDING.md`](../../openspec/changes/runtime-working-set-ownership/evidence/2026-10-01-boot-crash-loop-24bar-take/FINDING.md).

**2026-10-01 — `runtime-working-set-ownership` S2.2/S2.3/S2.4 CHECKED: each class is measured separately and §2's envelope is reported as it stands — the conservative sum does NOT fit, and the playback term is not what overflows it (measurement/report only; no firmware, no `src/`/`include/` change, no build, no device action).** [`S2C23-CLASS-BUDGET.md`](../../openspec/changes/runtime-working-set-ownership/S2C23-CLASS-BUDGET.md) charges the envelope `fixed + N*P + Cmax*C + Dmax*D + Imax*I + Omax*O + canonical + roots + undo + visual + standby + reserve`. **S2.2, each class separately:** `P` is the shared per-slot-runtime `RuntimePlaybackViewSet` (**831 KiB whole-take / 331 KiB windowed**, derived in `S2C1-PLAYBACK-WINDOW-LEASE.md`); `C` is **383 KiB** of *its own* lifetime class (b) — the six prewarms required during RECORDING (`canonicalPassInputs` 144, `frozenCompanionPasses` 96, `frozenCompanionApply` 66, `reconstruction` 64, `pairLookup` 10, `spans` 2) plus the transfer horizon, i.e. **not** a multiple of P and unmoved by P's derived capacity; `D` is **308 KiB** of class (c), capacity that must already exist at arm (`frozenCaptureCompanions` 80, `bridgeMap` 68, the two 80 KiB history vectors); `O` is ≤ **1 windowed P** per in-flight switch against S4b.2's *measured* **1 pool chunk** for the turn itself; **`I` is deliberately not sized here** (`Imax = 1` is §2's, but its byte figure belongs to the visual (S4e/S2.8) and undo owners). **Shared backing is charged once**, per §2's own rule: P, C and D all read the one view-set allocation. **S2.3, the envelope:** the pool is **8 MiB** and its ceiling is *measured* — the 24-bar heap runs refused `bytes=8192` at `live=8527KB`, and an allocator `FATAL` followed `external live 8144 KiB / 1176 blocks`. **2026-10-01 — `runtime-working-set-ownership` S2.1 CHECKED: the playback window lease is derived from the window instead of the 2048-event ceiling, and the `P` term is measured on the target ABI (derivation only; no firmware, no `src/`/`include/` change, no build, no device action).** S2.1 is the promotion of **RC-MEM-2's outstanding item** ("per-slot bundles are sized by the representable ceiling, not by the window"), and it is the term the budget multiplies by the derived N; it was blocked on phase F's contract interfaces, which **S4c.1 landed earlier this session**. [`S2C1-PLAYBACK-WINDOW-LEASE.md`](../../openspec/changes/runtime-working-set-ownership/S2C1-PLAYBACK-WINDOW-LEASE.md) records the derivation. **The composition:** `P` is one `RuntimePlaybackViewSet`, and the code already computes its total (`fixedExternalBytes()`, pinned by `test_runtime_view_set_prewarm_has_fixed_capacity_and_no_growth`), so the derivation is about its **inputs** — and those are measured on the **target ABI, not the host**: `MidiEvent` carries a `sysexData` pointer, so `sizeof(MidiEvent)` is **20 B on cortex-m7 and 32 B on x86-64**, and a host-derived figure would inflate every `P` figure by **34 %**. The sizes come from cross-compiling the real headers with the project's own toolchain (`arm-none-eabi-c++`, `-mcpu=cortex-m7 …`, the Teensy framework MIDI library), each value read out of the compiler. Result: **35 B/event** per view (the design's own figure, now verified on device), **29 B/event** for capture staging, **331 KiB per holder** windowed-only (the long-loop shape RC-MEM-2's release path produces) and **831 KiB** whole-take reserved. **Four exact cross-checks against existing authority figures verify the arithmetic:** `design.md`'s 35 B/event; `ExecutionBounds.md`'s views+bases **350.0 KiB**, bridges **360.0 KiB**, `captureStagings[2]` **61,952 B each** (59,392 + 128 × 20) and `canonicalPassInputs` **147,456 B at C=2048**. **The derivation:** capacity is the events the *resolved window* may hold (`eventsPerBar × windowBars`, at the design's ~72/bar typical and 4,096 refs/bar ceiling), not the global 2048 — and it is `min(declared product limit, windowEvents)`, because at the ceiling density a 2-bar window needs **8,192** events, *more* than today's ceiling, so the window sets the shape and a declared limit must set the size. A 2-bar window at typical density is **28.6 KB**, ~**12×** smaller than today (1 bar: 20×), which is what makes `N × P` affordable rather than merely paid; and length independence becomes a property of the formula, since nothing in it references the loop length. **One coincidence is named rather than conflated:** `design.md` Revision 11's "~325 KB per loop, ~2.6 MB at N = 8" is the **`N × whole-root`** term — the published snapshot root, a *different* structure — and its closeness to this one (331 KiB) is exactly why the two must not be treated as the same term. **Owed and named:** the **product limit** value (what one interval may capture — the decision RC-MEM-2's own record called "the decision to take"); **`N`** itself (S2.3/S2.4, provisional per phase F); and C3(a)'s per-slot saturation claim (`committedEvents + intervalHorizon`) with the `C`/`D`/`I` classes, which are **S2.2/S2.3**'s measurements. **Verification:** no code changed, so no red-proof applies and no build or upload was needed; the formula this derivation sizes recomputes from the `sizeof`s, so a capacity edit cannot silently change the figure without that pinned fixture seeing it. `openspec validate --strict` valid. **S3 gates therefore rests on two items:** **S2b.7(a)**'s third conjunct (a track playing at the same blocking-drain edge — an arrangement, not a wait) and **S2.2/S2.3**.

**2026-10-01 — `runtime-working-set-ownership` S4c.1 CHECKED: the interval/window readiness and immutable-currency specification for the sibling is written, and it unblocks S2.1 (specification only; no firmware, no build, no device action).** S4c.1's job is to turn `design.md` **Revision 11** ("immutable readiness at re-entry, not whole-loop publication") and its row 11 into acceptance criteria a sibling can be held to **without changing this change's publication unit** — and it is the item the remaining half of S3 gates was waiting on, because the `P` class *is* the playback window lease that S2.1 may create only once the phase-F contract's interfaces exist. **2026-10-01 — `runtime-working-set-ownership`: two device-state defects fixed on the way to S4b.9's clause, and the clause itself observed on hardware (firmware + host tooling; image `a1f4e4c0…`, RAM1 unchanged at `variables 96,192`).** **(1) A corrupt head prefix no longer costs the ring.** `captures/s4b-gate-newimage-01` recorded `RING,head_bad,1,op=4,head=604322,tail=613846,used=9524,type=55,plen=12588,prefix=37322c313030…` — with the header layout (`CaptureRecordHeader` = `{type, payloadLen}` plus a pad byte) those fields are provably read out of *text*, with a valid header exactly **7 bytes later**, while `head + used == tail` still held: the structure was self-consistent, the bytes were not, and the blunt whole-ring reset discarded **9 524 readable bytes** and invalidated the capture, aborting an unrelated leg. The fix is a bounded resynchronization (`headResyncDropBytes`, ≤256 B scan, a candidate accepted only when the record after it is plausible, the loss counted and named `RING,head_resync,…`, the walk still draining the intact records, and the wipe kept as the fallback). Regression on the same three-switch leg: `captures/s4b-gate-newimage-02` has `wiped=0`, `head_bad=0`, `integrity: COMPLETE` and **two commits** with an empty warning list. **(2) A receipt no longer waits for the stop.** With the ring healthy the leg still refused at the successor gate; the device's own rows say why — `captures/s4b9-cross-track-18` has the `PERS,result` receipt 3.1 s (device time) after the record stop while the harness's 25 s wait expired, and `-20` shows a 120 s wait expiring with the row in the capture. The ring is **retained, not drained, under transport** by design, so a gesture that keeps a track playing throughout holds the receipt until after the stop — after its consumer has moved on. **2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.6c: the interval index over pinned bodies — and **task 3.6 checked** (firmware).** `RetainedIntervalIndex` is one **bit per bar** ("any pinned body carries content here"): a **descriptor**, never an event copy — `TickIndex`'s whole-history copy storage is deliberately not inherited, and `CommittedEventRange` stays the body-reading primitive. It publishes **atomically with the source revision** (a candidate built and swapped by one assignment, the revision stamped inside it), its **update strategy is a full rebuild per admitted revision** (both the old and the new affected ranges covered by construction, no reader ever holding a mutated index), its **resident bound** is `kRetainedIndexMaxBars = 512` bars (16 words) with a **named refusal** beyond it — an index that answered part of a loop would present the complete scan as window-bounded, so that scan's accounting stays in admission — and its **lifetime** is the revision it describes (a query for another revision is `RevisionMismatch`, never a stale answer). The fixture also builds an interval from the **pinned chunk lists alone**, so "no resident whole-loop root" is demonstrated rather than asserted. **2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.11: the shared-view ownership rules and the transition table (DEC-108 §13d) — 3.7's first dependency is now green (firmware; task 3.11 checked).** The ownership rules are stated as **one table**: `PlaybackViewTransition` (the spec's seven transitions: new edit, slot switch, selected-track change, stop-with-successor-start, transport stop, clear/load, late completion) → `PlaybackViewTransitionEffect` (one field per clause the spec names) → `resolvePlaybackViewTransition`, the **pure** resolution, so the table has a single implementation and a fixture pins every row — including the invariant asserted for **all seven**: no lifecycle transition may tear the served window. The application is `Track::applyPlaybackViewTransition` (cancels the candidate and/or retires the prepared successor per row, invalidates the operation identity per row, never touches the served window) with `Track::playbackViewRoleStateForSlot` as the role state a slice asserts with, and the **publication guard**: a build records its **operation generation** where it begins, so a completion arriving after that identity moved is refused and releases **only its own candidate** — a late completion publishes nothing. Generation-qualified identity is now load-bearing: clear/load bumps it, so returning to a slot revives nothing. *Verification:* focused **55/55**, full native **2686 / 2679 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, `teensy41-capture-serial` **SUCCESS** on a clean rebuild with RAM1 `variables 96,192` **unchanged** / `code 391,928 + padding 1,288` (448 B headroom) and **no re-base** — the S3.0 pin is **unchanged** at 6,512 because the 4-byte field fitted existing padding on both ABIs. Three mutations red-proved with byte-identical restores (the publication guard dropped; the identity not invalidated on clear/load; the table's continuing rows made to cancel the candidate). *One attempted mutation did **not** discriminate, and that is recorded rather than dropped:* emptying the explicit prepared-successor **retirement** branch leaves the suite green, because `RuntimePlaybackViewBuild::discard()` clears its own destination's `complete` and after a successor publication that destination *is* the view the `ready` role holds — the cancel already retires the lookahead for this lane's sequencing. That branch covers a `ready` view the current builder is **not** pointing at, which the fixture does not construct: a **named gap**, deferred to 3.7 where the successor lane gains a production caller — and the packet's mutation cell was corrected to say exactly that. **3.7's remaining dependencies:** 3.12 (admission limit + bounded legacy path), 3.13 (preview), 3.14 (undo/redo audible handoff) and 4.5 (fault recovery). **2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.6a (DEC-108 items 4/12(a)/13(a)): a retained source revision is held in explicit roles, protected on both destruction paths, and released by one predicate (firmware; task 3.6 stays open).** The first clause of 3.6 is green. `RetainedPlaybackSource` — an identity `(revision, generation)` plus **descriptor pins** and **owned bodies** — lives in explicit **serving / candidate / retiring** roles on the per-slot runtime, admitted by `Track::retainPlaybackSourceForSlot` with typed outcomes (`Admitted`, `AlreadyRetained`, `NoRuntime`, `NotServable`, `RoleCapacityReached`: the bound refuses **by name** rather than discarding a still-needed source, item 13(a)). **`tryReleaseRetainedPlaybackSource` is the one release predicate** — the revision advanced past it, no window serves it, no builder holds a frozen source, no closure obligation is outstanding, or the content it described is gone — and the retention is a **named term of `Track::noLiveOwnerForSlot`**. Both destruction paths are covered, each by the mechanism that decides it: the **reclamation consumer** reads the retained pins (`TrackManager::reclaimUnreferencedDisabledPasses` merges them into the set the loop consumes, because "a pin registered only alongside undo references is not sufficient protection"), and the **direct reset/replacement path** is safe by **body ownership** — `LoopEventStore::retainChunkRefs` means the eleven `Loop::resetPassTimeline` call sites need **no veto**, so gestures keep working while the bodies survive and are returned only by the release predicate. That ownership **superseded** the approved veto mechanism for this slice, and it is the spec's own "actual body ownership" clause rather than a relaxation. Verification: focused **52/52**, full native **2683 / 2676 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, `teensy41-capture-serial` **SUCCESS** on a clean rebuild with RAM1 `variables 96,192` **unchanged** / `code 391,864 + padding 1,352` / locals 34,880 (floor 840; **336 B more headroom than the 3.5 baseline**) and **no re-base**; three mutations red-proved with byte-identical restores (sha256 verified). Two implementation findings are recorded: the **S3.0 size pin is now per ABI** (6,368 → **6,464** on the target, 6,544 on the host — the holder contains pointer-sized pin lists, and the first build failed on the target only), and the enlarged cold reclamation pass moved to FLASH with its TU's existing macro, which **returned 336 B of ITCM**. **Still open in 3.6, named not implied:** the **interval index over pinned bodies** (later intervals from the retained revision, no resident whole-loop root, both affected ranges, atomic publication with the source revision, inspected-work budgeting) and the **lag rule** (F-3: one pass late and only that, the named second-miss breach, the allowance not reset by a further edit, the consumer never blocked). **2026-10-01 — `runtime-working-set-ownership` S4b.6 + S4b.7 PARTIAL: a switch's inbound occupancy now has one off-clock owner and the commit binds to it without taking it; the *demoted* target shape is measured and owed (firmware; RAM1 +16 B ITCM, no new RAM1 state — no upload was performed).** S4b.6 asked that the switch bind to the target slot's **occupancy** with no allocation on either hot path; S4b.7 names who may take that occupancy instead, and the stage's risk is that each half alone produces the opposite failure (`slotIfAllocated` alone ⇒ a **silently dead** switch; provisioning alone ⇒ allocation on a MIDI edge or the clock). **Landed:** `Track::ensurePlaybackMergedEventsForSlot` binds through `playbackRuntime.slotIfAllocated` and is a documented **no-op** when the slot has no runtime, with the predicate named beside it (`Track::hasPlaybackOccupancyForSlot`); the commit branch in `TrackManager::updateAllTracks` keeps the switch **pending** when the inbound occupancy is absent, instead of committing into a slot whose runtime does not exist; and provisioning is the new idempotent off-clock owner `TrackManager::provisionSlotForSwitch`, reached through the **existing** deferred request owner (`requestSlotSwitch` → `requestDeferredPlaybackPrewarm` → `main.cpp`'s deferred frame provisions then prewarms), refusing with its own `OperationKind::SlotSwitch` (`op=slot_switch`) because the refusal contract is "the switch stays pending", not "the request is dropped". **The entry's eligibility worry does not materialise, and the reason is not the predicate it named:** the prewarm consumer is **not** gated by `hasRealtimeIdleWork` (that belongs to the maintenance scan); what bounds it is the deferred frame's shape — the prewarm slot sits after the frame's early return while a deferred overdub stop is outstanding, and the mark is cleared **only** by the take — so a switch beside a finalizing predecessor provisions on the first eligible turn *after* that finalization retires: a bounded delay, not a dead end (changing that ordering is S4b.2's stage). **Fixtures** (both on the production press route, not a direct `requestSlotSwitch`): `test_s4b_6_a_switch_to_a_slot_without_occupancy_provisions_off_clock` (one bar) and `test_s4b_6_a_switch_to_a_multi_bar_target_without_occupancy_also_provisions_off_clock` (8 bars), each driving the real lane pair (`takeDeferredPlaybackPrewarm` → `provisionSlotForSwitch` → `ensurePlaybackMergedEventsForSlot`). **Red-proved twice, each restored byte-identically:** replacing the occupancy term with `false` fails both at *"the switch may not commit before its occupancy exists"* (`Expected 0 Was 2` — the commit landed early into a slot with no runtime); reverting the binding to `trySlot` fails both at *"the MIDI edge must not provision inline"*. **A measurement that changed the fixture, not the code:** a forced `TRACK_PLAYING` plus `selectSlot` leaves `lastTickInLoop` at `0` across 5,576 ticks, so no loop-end wrap is ever detected and a queued switch can never be *due*; the fixtures therefore reach the production playing state through an overdub **start** on a populated slot (that is what enables it, plays it and publishes its pair) and retire the predecessor's finalizer **before** the press, because a live finalizer freezes the playhead (the S4b.1 finding) and would hide the term under test. **OWED, measured, and not a missing fixture: the demoted target.** With a 24-bar target (`> kMaxDetailedWindowBars × TICKS_PER_BAR` = 12,288 ticks) carrying bar-spread committed content, the switch is **still pending** after the off-clock owner has taken its occupancy (`ready=0 occ=1 pending=1`), because the commit's long-loop hold term (`isPlaybackMergedMidiEventsReadyForSlot`) requires a **non-empty** windowed `mergedMidiEvents` and the windowed gather (`Loop::tryGatherPublishedSnapshotEventsInWindow`) holds the window *empty* (`GatherMissHoldEmpty`) unless a published root supplies it — the review's "silent dead switch" on that shape, as a **readiness** question rather than an occupancy one. It needs either a published-root fixture on the windowed publication lane (S4c/F) or an architect decision to relax the hold; both committed fixture shapes stay deliberately below the demotion bound and say so in their doc block. **2026-10-01 — `runtime-working-set-ownership` S4b.1's finding (a) is discharged, and its "press dropped" reading is corrected: the retention carrier exists and the new reproducer covers the denied path (test-only; no `src/` change).** (a) recorded "when `Track::stopOverdubbing` denies admission on capacity, the switch returns `false` and the press is **dropped** rather than retained". Reading the gesture instead of the note: `MidiButtonActions::handleToggleRecordForSlot` calls `finalizeCaptureAndSelectSlot`, and when it returns false the empty-target branch calls `TrackManager::retainRecordStartForSlot(trackIdx, slotIndex)` and logs "Track %d loop %d: switch and record start retained (stop not yet admitted)" — so the retained carrier (a) asked for is already implemented. New `test_s4b_1_a_denied_stop_on_an_uncommitted_switch_retains_the_targets_start` is that path's reproducer: another slot's admitted finalization occupies the track's single finalization capacity (DEC-078 item 6), the switch's predecessor then captures live beside it (the required outgoing-finalizer + incoming-capture overlap) and *its* stop is **denied**; the fixture asserts the active slot does not move, the target's start **is** retained (`isRecordingQueued`), the predecessor's stop **is** accepted-and-latched against its own slot, the occupant's job and lease are untouched and the predecessor keeps capturing — then that retiring the occupant's finalization and turning the lanes makes the retained start **execute with no further gesture** (target active and recording, latch cleared, nothing stolen). **Red-proved twice, each restored byte-identically:** dropping `retainRecordStartForSlot` from the gesture fails this fixture (*"the target's start must be retained, not dropped with the gesture"*), the sibling repeated-switch fixture and the two existing retention fixtures — so the retention is load-bearing on the **denied** path as well as the admitted one; dropping the denied-stop latch fails this fixture at *"Expected 0 Was 1. an uncommitted switch must not move the active slot"*, i.e. the **latch** is what holds the active slot in place — what (a) read as "the press was dropped" was the S4f.5 protection working, and nothing here is a defect to fix. **The real remainder, with its prerequisite measured:** a **populated** target does not take the record carrier at all — the gesture queues a **playback** switch (`queuePlayingSlotSwitch` → the state machine's pending switch plus `pendingSlotEnabled`), and that queued switch commits in the **multi-slot-commit lane inside `TrackManager::updateAllTracks`** (the production per-tick entry). Driving that entry from this suite **fails to link**, for exactly four symbols: `Track::playMidiEvents(uint32_t, bool)`, `Track::playMidiEventsForSlot(uint8_t, uint32_t, bool)`, `TrackManager::isTrackAudible(uint8_t) const`, `Track::shouldCommitQueuedPlaybackStart(uint32_t) const`. Extending the shared harness's linked closure for those four — the `HARNESS_LINKS_*` pattern, without shadowing them in the fail-closed stub surface — is therefore the **prerequisite for the S4b.5/S4b.6/S4b.7 fixtures**, because that lane is where a queued switch actually commits and where the review's "silent dead switch" risk lives; driving only the dispatch helpers the suite already links cannot see it. **2026-09-30 — the mixed leg (record predecessor, seeded overdub successor) landed: its plan, its own preparation branch, the composed steps **and** its own grading mode, each as its own verified slice (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** The spec's *Mixed record predecessor and overdub successor* scenario ("a record interval A stops and seeded B begins overdubbing while A finalizes") is the two recipes composed, not a third: `leg_gestures("mixed")` is `select_track → a_record_start → b_switch → b_overdub_start → b_stop_request`, with A's start the **record** capture of 4.2 and B's successor the **overdub** of 4.3. The difference from the record leg is exactly the firmware's carrier rule — B **has** committed passes, so `handleToggleRecordForSlot`'s S4f.6 carrier (`!track.hasCommittedPassesInSlot`) does not apply, the switch stops A and selects B, and B's start then takes its own record-control press — and preparation is the leg's own branch (`seed_take(B)` → `prepare_empty(A)` → `require_idle(A)`, A last so it is the selected target), because a seeded A would make A's press an overdub and an armed A would consume the start press (`handleArmedRecordPress` cancels an arm under a running transport). The driven steps compose the two verified sequences unchanged, and the wrapper CLI accepts `--leg mixed`. **The grading mode is the second half:** `analyse(leg="mixed")` reads A with the **record** vocabulary (its `RECS` stop, `reentry_window_open`, `canonical_release`) beside B with the **overdub** families (its `DIAG,reentry,admit` start, `stop_state` execution, release), the route span runs from A's record stop to B's admission with the **capture-switch** as the production row (no carrier, since B is populated), and the identity link asks for **B's chain only** — a conforming mixed run is not failed for lacking an overdub chain on A. Each site is explicit about which mode's rows it reads, and the first *slice* of this work refused to grade the leg at all rather than grade it with the wrong vocabulary; that refusal is now replaced by the mode. Evidence: `test_accepted_sequence` **151/151** (13 new across the two halves — 6 flow, 7 grading), corpus **3/3** (every retained fixture keeps its verdict, so the record and overdub modes are untouched by the condition changes), scenario 38/38, authorization 24/24, `test_retention_handoff_plan` 33/33, host sweep **1,068 tests / 75 suites** re-measured 2026-10-01 (single-process `unittest discover` over `scripts/test_*.py`, identical per-module) with only the pre-existing failing suites — six, none of which imports this change's modules — and **8 mutations red-proved** with byte-identical, sha256-verified restores (4 flow: B's overdub start dropped, B's stop turned into a record press, A's idle requirement removed, the oracle refusal removed; 4 grading: A's stop read with the binding vocabulary, A's overdub chain required again, the production row read with the record carrier vocabulary, the execution link not computed for the mixed leg). **What remains:** registration (`accepted_sequence_mixed` + preset) so the runner route reaches the leg the CLI already accepts, the mixed **stimulus profile** with its own declared authorization (A empty + B seeded — the spec's "record and overdub fixtures MUST have different verified content preconditions"), and the device leg with the rest of 6.x under a per-session authorization. **2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 5.2 landed: content parity, the timing gates and the run's own teardown are now requirements of the acceptance verdict, each able to veto it, with the evidence read from the owner that already decides it (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** Design decision 6 asks for "content parity and the existing timing gates" in the conjunction and keeps the shutdown result "an independent field [that] can veto overall success", and says "PASS only for the complete conjunction". **The reader layer is new and deliberately thin:** `hitl/acceptance_evidence.py` answers three questions in its owners' own words — content parity from `hitl.library_manifest.compare_manifests`' report (`pass`/`verdict` plus the unexplained manifest/lifecycle and count differences), the timing half through the timing owner's own `midi_boundary_timing_issues(summary)` (so an issue the timing owner learns to name vetoes without a second edit), and the teardown from `hitl.device_shutdown`'s record — and it never re-implements a check. **`analyse(..., inputs=…)` grades the three as checks:** `content_parity` (kind `content`) and `timing_gates` (kind `timing`) fail as `ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_FAIL`, an incomplete drain is a **setup** failure (`SETUP_INCOMPLETE`: a run that did not drain is not verdict-grade, which is how the sealed bundle's own rule already reads it), and **not supplied** is `UNKNOWN` — so an older capture can still be graded but can never be passed. **Both entry points read the same evidence:** the oracle CLI gained `--content-report`/`--timing-report` (the teardown rides `--run-report`'s own `shutdown`), the scenario's `_EVIDENCE_VALUE_FLAGS` carries all four, and the retained excerpt is now pinned *three* ways through both routes — supplied ⇒ `ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_PASS`, not supplied ⇒ `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, never-staged ⇒ a non-pass. **Two real defects were found and fixed, neither caused by this slice:** `ShutdownResult.as_dict()` omitted `ok` while `hitl.reporting.derive_verdict` requires exactly that key, so a *real* run's sealed bundle could never pass on teardown however cleanly it drained; and running the oracle as a script put `scripts/hitl` on `sys.path[0]`, where `scripts/hitl/serial/` answers `import serial` and broke any verifier that transitively needs the serial stack — which is why the timing adapter imports its owner lazily and reports an unimportable owner as `UNKNOWN` *with the reason*, never as a pass. **Evidence:** `test_accepted_sequence` **140/140** (8 new `VetoTests`: a failing content comparison vetoes and quotes the owner's own difference; a report with no verdict is a gap; a timing issue vetoes naming the owner's own issue (`capture_ring_overflow`, `unexpected_midi_input_call_site`); an incomplete drain is a setup failure; absent evidence can never pass; the real-run teardown record satisfies the bundle rule while the pre-fix shape does not; the adapters are readers, not re-implementations), corpus **3/3** with every retained fixture keeping its verdict, scenario **38/38**, the neighbours green (`test_retention_handoff_plan` 33/33, `test_hitl_correlated_actions` 23/23, authorization 24/24), host sweep **1,067 tests / 75 suites** with only the seven pre-existing failures (`test_midi_clock` failed once mid-sweep and passed on re-run, standalone three times and in the repeated sweep: an observed flake, recorded not hidden), and a CLI check on the retained device excerpt (supplied ⇒ PASS with all three `ok`; a failing content report ⇒ `ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_FAIL`, quoting `{'track': 7, 'slot': 4, 'field': 'hasData'}`). **Owed to 6.3:** a live run whose bundle actually carries the three reports — and, for the content half, the per-interval inventory the content pipeline records rather than the library-level manifest comparison used here. [ACCEPTANCE-VETO-EXECUTION.md](../../openspec/changes/response-driven-hitl-acceptance/ACCEPTANCE-VETO-EXECUTION.md).

**2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 4.3 landed: the overdub leg's three clauses are checked on both sides, and a switch answered by the playback queue is refused at the press (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** The recipe was already the retention prefix (confirmed seeds, the proven single capture-switch, B's `Overdubbing started @ tick` gate, one B stop request), so this slice is the *checking*. **The switch step is now a route wait** — the same `_await_route` 4.2 introduced — whose production route is the capture-switch's own row (`Loop B: Switch gesture from slot A`) and whose conflict vocabulary makes `Queued`/`Reaffirmed playback switch` `CONTRADICTED`: the leg stops **at the press** with `PLAYBACK_REAFFIRMED_INSTEAD_OF_SWITCH` and sends nothing else, where the old wait *accepted* the playback row as its confirmation and left the refusal to the next gesture's `_switch_pending` guard (that press was already spent by then). **"No separate A stop" is read twice:** the plan carries no A stop and no A slot note before B's, and the oracle counts A's own stop press as a *second* request for A, so `L7_one_press_per_stop` fails on it. **"No wait for predecessor retirement" is pinned behaviourally:** a driven leg whose capture retires A **nowhere** (no `canonical_release`, no `Reentry released slot=3`, no pending-switch row) still reaches `DROVE_LEG`, so no critical-window wait depends on the release edge. **The oracle reads the same route:** `L5b_b_start_route` (added for 4.2) now covers both legs with each leg's own vocabulary — for the overdub leg the route rows are the **press** rows themselves and the *first* one decides, because they are mutually exclusive at that press: the capture-switch row ⇒ `ok`; a playback row first **with B's overdub start admitted** ⇒ `fail` (B started, but through the playback route — the substitute design decision 5 refuses); a playback row with **no** start ⇒ `unknown` (a capture that never got that far is the existing L5 gap, which is why the pinned `s4f13-od4-*` fixture keeps its `SETUP_INCOMPLETE` verdict); neither ⇒ `unknown`. A later playback row (B's own stop press can queue one) is not the route decision, the same precedence rule the record leg applies to its carrier row. On the retained device capture `s4f22-dec096-od-13` the check reads **ok** and names the row it read (`[57.162] [INFO] Loop 5: Switch gesture from slot 4`), so the production route is confirmed on real evidence, not only on synthetic chains. **Evidence:** `test_accepted_sequence` **132/132** (6 new: the recipe driving with no retirement anywhere, the playback re-affirmation refused at the press with the pressed-gesture list asserted, the capture-switch as the production route, a playback route that carried B failing, a playback row without a start staying a gap, and a separate A stop failing L7), corpus **3/3** (including `s4f13-od4-*`), scenario 38/38, authorization 24/24, `test_retention_handoff_plan` 33/33, `test_hitl_correlated_actions` 23/23, host sweep **1,059 tests / 75 suites** with only the seven pre-existing failures, **4 mutations red-proved** with byte-identical restores — and one attempted mutation recorded as an *equivalence* rather than a coverage gap (adding the playback row to the flow's accept set changes nothing, because `CorrelatedGesture.consider` checks the conflict vocabulary before the stage's own wires). Firmware untouched, so native/build/RAM1 are not implicated. **4.3 stays `[~]` for its device leg (6.3),** as 4.2: the route vocabulary is read from the firmware's own emitters and the retained capture, and a driven leg is what confirms it. [OVERDUB-RECIPE-EXECUTION.md](../../openspec/changes/response-driven-hitl-acceptance/OVERDUB-RECIPE-EXECUTION.md).

**2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 4.2 landed: the record recipe is switch-carried, its targets must be genuinely empty *and idle*, and a playback/overdub answer is a named wrong route rather than a substitute (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** The record leg used to stop the global transport as A's stop — the very thing the spec's *Record successor* scenario forbids ("global transport does not stop") and the thing task 5.1's window predicate now fails — so the plan is `select_track → a_record_start → b_switch_start → b_stop`, where **one** slot gesture carries both edges. The firmware is the reason it can: `MidiButtonActions::handleToggleRecordForSlot` selects the target, finalizes A's capture through `finalizeCaptureAndSelectSlot`, and — because the target has no committed passes (`!track.hasCommittedPassesInSlot`) — *queues* B's record start in the same gesture, or **retains** it when A's stop is accepted but not yet admitted (S4f.6/S4f.3). **Preparation is now split by leg:** `prepare_empty` (4.1's census → scoped clear → `CLEARED`/`ALREADY_EMPTY`) prepares **both** targets for the record leg and seeds nothing (`seed_take` is the overdub leg's), B is prepared first so that A is the *selected* target when the leg starts, and `require_idle` refuses a target the clear left armed or recording — because the firmware's own `handleArmedRecordPress` *cancels* an arm under a running transport, so driving on would silently consume the recipe's start press. **The recipe's waits observe the device's own rows** (`_await_record_route`, over task 3.1's four-stage `CorrelatedGesture`): A's record start (immediate, quantized or punch-in) **and** its slot-scoped `RECORDING` execution, so a start queued on the loop-phase boundary is seen through its execution; the switch's carrier row (or its retained twin, which is legitimate and no longer trips the overdub leg's retained-switch guard); and B's single stop. A playback/overdub answer is a **named** `WRONG_MODE_ROUTE`, an uncarried switch is `SWITCH_NOT_CARRIED` / `B_RECORD_START_UNCONFIRMED`, and the wait never presses, so a wrong route costs no second gesture. **The oracle reads the same vocabulary** as the new `L5b_b_start_route` over the **route decision span** (A's accepted record stop → B's record start): a carrier row is `ok`, a wrong-route row with no carrier is `fail`, and neither is `unknown` (never a pass) — the span matters, because a *later* `Playback started` is `PendingSwitchGate`'s own "the switch landed" marker and is not a wrong route. The stale reading that a record stop "publishes inline, so no window is the expected shape" was corrected against this firmware's deferred record-stop obligation (`retainRecordStopGeometryObligation`), so the spec's "single stop acceptance during A's ownership window" applies to the record leg too. **Evidence:** `test_accepted_sequence` **126/126** (15 new: the recipe's receipts, a quantized start seen through its execution, a retained carrier, an early retirement that does not stop the leg, two wrong-mode routes, both halves of an uncarried switch, the oracle's carrier/wrong-route/span/absence readings, and two preparation pins — an armed target refused, and a populated A that cannot be cleared stopping the run before any gesture), corpus **3/3**, `test_accepted_sequence_scenario` 38/38, `test_hitl_stimulus_authorization` 24/24, `test_retention_handoff_plan` 33/33, `test_hitl_correlated_actions` 23/23, host sweep **1,053 tests / 75 suites** with only the seven pre-existing unrelated failures, **8 mutations red-proved** with byte-identical restores — one of which *survived the first run* (the route span), which is why the span-boundary test now asserts `unknown` with no carrier present. Firmware untouched, so native/build/RAM1 are not implicated. **4.2 stays `[~]` for its device leg (6.3):** the accept vocabulary is read from the firmware's own emitters and has never been confirmed on real rows, which is also where a firmware that does *not* carry the start would surface as `SWITCH_NOT_CARRIED`. [RECORD-RECIPE-EXECUTION.md](../../openspec/changes/response-driven-hitl-acceptance/RECORD-RECIPE-EXECUTION.md).

**2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 5.1's window invariants landed: the spec's *Continuously playing acceptance window* is now two oracle predicates read over the driver's own boundary, so a transport stop or a clock-source change inside a measured window yields the specified non-PASS (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** Task 5.1 had named the gap itself — "transport stop and clock change" were the two edges with no predicate — and the spec's requirement sentence is where the boundary comes from: *"Preparation, clearing, seeding and final stopped-only verification SHALL have explicit boundaries outside that window"*. **The window is therefore the driver's own mark pair, not a guess.** `hitl/flows/accepted_sequence.py`'s `drive_leg` records `leg_window_end_row` **when the leg's plan returned** (`LegOutcome`, alongside `leg_start_row` taken just before the first gesture), and the run scope writes both into its report, so a verdict names the span it was read over. That position is load-bearing, measured on real data — in `captures/s4f22-dec096-od-13` the leg's last press is at device 59.141 s while the driver's final `Transport stopped` lands at 67.747 s, 8 s and thousands of device rows later, because the settle and the final stopped-only stop are the run's *teardown*: grading that capture through the oracle CLI with the flow's mark is **`ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_PASS`**, and with a mark taken after the run's own end it is **`ACCEPTED_SEQUENCE_FAIL`** on the run's own final stop (the first version of the slice had exactly that bug, and the capture is what showed it). **What the predicates read is the device's vocabulary:** `continuous_transport` over `ClockManager`'s `Transport stopped` human row (written straight to `Serial`, so its absence is live evidence) and `clock_source_stable` over `DebugSessionCapture::clockSource`'s `#CAP,<us>,CS,<from>,<to>` one-shot, whose meaning is that the evidence either side is not one timeline. **Absence is graded as absence:** no run marks falls back to the leg's own `Loop N:` stop-request rows *and says so* in `evidence["window"]` (two rows minimum — one bounds nothing), and a capture that cannot bound the window reports both predicates `UNKNOWN` (⇒ `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`), never `OK`. The shed rule is scoped **to the window**: `CS` is ordinary (non-Tier-A) ring text, so a row dropped inside the span makes absence non-evidence, while a drop outside it cannot make the span unmeasurable — measured reason: the same run shed one ordinary row at device 51.4 s, before its leg began, and a capture-wide rule would have called that window's clock source unmeasurable for a drop that could not have touched it. **The record leg's consequence is stated, not inferred:** its plan still stops the global transport itself (`leg_gestures`' `a_stop`), contrary to the spec's *Record successor* scenario where the switch carries B's start, so a record-leg run fails `continuous_transport` and the oracle records a limitation naming the *plan* — which makes 4.2 measurable instead of prose. **Evidence:** `test_accepted_sequence` **112/112** (12 new pins: the fallback boundary, a stop inside and after the window, the run's marks as the boundary, a clock transition inside, shed rows inside vs outside, one press row not being a window, the malformed/absent mark shapes, the record-leg limitation, and the driver's own mark ordering), corpus **3/3** (every retained device fixture keeps its verdict), `test_accepted_sequence_scenario` 38/38, `test_hitl_stimulus_authorization` 24/24, `test_retention_handoff_plan` 33/33, full host sweep **1,039 tests / 75 suites** with only the seven pre-existing unrelated failures (none referencing this slice's modules; `test_note_edit_fader_motor_timing` is a standalone script with no `unittest` tests, i.e. a harness artifact rather than a failure), **7 mutations red-proved** with every file restored byte-identically, plus the real-capture CLI comparison above. Firmware untouched, so `pio test -e native`, the `teensy41-capture-serial` build and the RAM1 budget are not implicated. **5.1 stays `[~]`:** its predicates are in for both modes, but the record leg cannot pass them until 4.2 makes it switch-carried, and the requirement's *mixed* record-predecessor/overdub-successor leg is 4.3's. [WINDOW-INVARIANT-EXECUTION.md](../../openspec/changes/response-driven-hitl-acceptance/WINDOW-INVARIANT-EXECUTION.md).

**2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 4.4b landed and 4.4 is closed: the accepted-sequence leg sequence is a stateless flow, its session/authorization/report is a host run scope, and the standalone driver is an argument-compatible wrapper both entry points share (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** The design's sentence *"the standalone driver becomes an argument-compatible wrapper"* needed the ~700-line leg body out of `scripts/hitl_accepted_sequence.py` first, and that moved it into three owners: **the sequence** is `hitl/flows/accepted_sequence.py` (`drive_leg`: the bounded read-only census → scoped stopped preparation → the seeded takes → the gesture plan → the final stop and the counted read-back; the gestures stay **data**, every wait stays a narrow bounded observation, and the flow reaches no serial/verify/reporting layer); **the session, the authorization and the report** are `hitl/accepted_sequence_run.py` (`RunRequest` → `run_accepted_sequence`, with the milestone-discipline report that `od-08` made non-negotiable); **the CLI** is now 130 lines of parser plus `request_from_args`, unchanged flags, unchanged exit codes, unchanged artifact layout. **The ownership question 4.4a named is answered rather than deferred:** the stopped-only per-family counter read-back is the **session's** — `ManagedCaptureSession.identity_stat_lines` owns the request, its fence and the decode (which stays with the serial owner, `hitl.serial.protocol`) — so the flow calls one accessor instead of importing a layer that is closed to both a flow and a scenario. **Both entry points reach one implementation:** `host_midi_hitl.py run` → the registered scenario (intent plus the runner→CLI translation) → the wrapper → the run scope → the flow, and the standalone CLI → the run scope → the flow, with the scenario owning the one translation so the paths cannot drift. **How the move was verified *as a move*:** all 23 moved functions were diffed against `git show HEAD:` and 22 came out byte-identical (the 23rd differs only in a docstring word), which is how two *real* drifts were caught and fixed — the seed's arm gate must accept the printed `Loop N: Start Recording` row and a `RECORDING` state, not just an `ARMED` `DISP` row (measured `od-10`: the ring can lag the Serial row by seconds), and the report's census keys are the census's own 0-based firmware `(track, slot)` pairs, not the run's 1-based CLI numbering. **Evidence:** `test_accepted_sequence` **100/100** (two new pins — the printed-row arm receipt, and a run that dies after the census still leaving its milestone report), `test_accepted_sequence_scenario` **38/38** (six new flow-layer pins, including the counter read-back's owner and the wrapper's unchanged argument surface), `test_hitl_stimulus_authorization` **24/24** repointed to the run scope with the same refusals, the full host sweep **1,025 tests** with only the seven pre-existing unrelated failures (`test_foundation_runner`/`test_layered_verifiers` unchanged), `pio test -e native` **2,643 cases / 2,636 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, **7 mutations red-proved** with byte-identical restores — and two of those seven *survived the first run* (the seed's arm wires, the milestone write), which is why those two tests exist now. **Rejected alternative, recorded:** routing the wrapper literally through `hitl.runner.main` would re-parse an already-parsed, argument-compatible CLI and relocate the run's artifacts (the scenario writes `<out>/accepted-sequence-<leg>`), changing a verified contract for no functional gain. asks for separate record and overdub scenarios in the existing registry, with unsupported legacy combinations rejected explicitly. **Registration.** `hitl/registry.py` gains `accepted_sequence_rec` **2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 4.1's host half landed: the run-scoped target authorization manifest is declared, enforced and recorded, so an unauthorized target stops a run before it mutates anything (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** Task 4's precondition names a *target authorization manifest* as a required run input, and the packet had already routed it to the stimulus registry (which declares each profile's recipe, and whose `stimulus list` is the mandated discovery path). **The declaration lives with the recipe.** `hitl/stimuli/spec.py` gains `Authorization` — the 1-based track, the slots a run may mutate, and the **provenance** of the grant (required, because an authorization nobody can trace is not one); an empty scope is a deliberate read-only profile, every number is range-checked, and `violations()` names the offending target *and* the declared scope. `StimulusSpec.authorization` is optional, so a profile that declares nothing cannot authorize a run — the checker refuses it by name rather than falling back to "no declaration, no check". `registry.py` declares the scope once for the two profiles these legs drive (track 8, slots 4/5 — the bench target the recorded `s4f13-*`/`s4f22-dec096-*` runs actually used, narrowed from the user's standing authorization of 2026-09-30), exposes it through `authorization_for`, and `stimulus list` now shows `targets=track 8 slots 4,5` / `targets=undeclared` per profile; a session that needs another bench scope forks the profile (`temporary_variant(..., authorization=…)`) instead of widening the canonical one, and the YAML view exports it as an indented block sequence. **The enforcement is the new module.** `hitl/stimuli/authorization.py` resolves `--authorization <stimulus-id>|cli` into the record the run is driven under: a manifest that does not cover the run's targets, an id the registry does not know, and a profile with no declaration are each an `AuthorizationRefused` carrying the record — never a traceback, because the refusal has to be legible evidence. The explicit CLI targets stay the compatibility path (`cli`, the default) and are recorded as *such* rather than silently unchecked. **Both drivers stop before the board.** `hitl_accepted_sequence.py` and `hitl_retention_handoff.py` resolve the authorization at the top of `main` — before the latch-refusing reset, before the re-upload, before the read-only census and before any MIDI gesture — write `result = "UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET"` with the refused target and the authorized scope into the same report they write on every other exit, and exit 3. **The record reaches the sealed bundle:** the oracle copies the run's `authorization` record into `reporting.build_report_bundle`'s section, so a sealed verdict names the scope it was driven under instead of leaving that section empty (new spec scenario *Target outside the run's authorization*). **Evidence:** new `scripts/test_hitl_stimulus_authorization.py` **24/24** (shape and range rules, the registry declarations and listing, the three checker inputs, and the drivers' refusal — with a reset-step sentinel that makes a revision which lost the guard fail loudly instead of flashing the board in a host test), `test_accepted_sequence` **98/98** (the bundle carries the authorization), the neighbouring 19-suite set green together, the full host sweep **987 tests / 74 suites** with only the seven pre-existing unrelated failures, `pio test -e native` **2,643 cases / 2,636 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, **six mutations** red-proved with every file restored byte-identically, `openspec validate response-driven-hitl-acceptance --strict` valid and `git diff --check` clean. Firmware untouched, so the `teensy41-capture-serial` build and RAM1 gates are not implicated by this slice. **4.1 stays `[~]`:** its device legs (target selection, the RAM/SD census, persistence-completion proof and a repeat without a reset) still need a per-session upload/target authorization.

**2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 3.3 closed: a run's verdict is now a sealed, versioned bundle that replays without a device, and the observation wait has one owner outside the gate (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** Three clauses, each landed. **(1) Immutable versioned report schema.** `hitl/reporting.py` now owns the **sealed bundle** next to the progress report: `BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` with a fixed section list, a sha256 `digest` over everything else, `write_report_bundle` sealing **once** (atomic rename, refuses to overwrite, checks version/digest/sections before writing), and one rule — `derive_verdict`, re-run by the reader — for the verdict: every recorded predicate ok **and** a teardown result present and ok, with a caller's success claim required to be backed by both, so "shutdown failure SHALL prevent overall success" is enforced rather than restated and a claim its own evidence denies is recorded as `bundle_verdict` instead of carried. **(2) The managed metadata path and verify-only replay without ports.** `hitl/run_metadata.run_identity` is the one identity builder behind both `metadata.json` and a bundle's `identity` section; `scripts/hitl_report_replay.py --bundle <path>` reads a sealed bundle and re-derives its verdict with no MIDI or serial port (pinned by patching `mido.open_output`/`serial.Serial` to raise), exiting 0 for a pass, 2 for an intact non-pass and 3 for a bundle that cannot be trusted (unknown version, content that no longer hashes, or a verdict its evidence denies) — and it states its own limit honestly: a digest is integrity, not a signature, so what it defeats is a bundle that *silently* disagrees with itself. The oracle seals the acceptance verdict: `hitl/accepted_sequence_probe.py --emit-bundle … [--run-report …]` turns each check into a predicate (`UNKNOWN` counted as not-ok, because an absent required edge is not a pass) and carries the run's `shutdown`, so a pass needs a proven drain; setup failure, protocol absence, teardown failure and a legitimate non-pass are each a recorded shape. **(3) The import gate, resolved without widening it.** The *observation* wait (rows the device emits on its own) is now one owner — `hitl/actions/observation.py::await_markers`, bounded, cancel-aware, ring-flush on the caller's cadence, injectable clock — wrapped by both drivers' `_await_markers`/`_wait_for_any`; it lives under `hitl.actions`, a prefix flows may already import, so no forbidden prefix was relaxed and the gate suite now pins that (facade under an allowed prefix, a flow importing it passes, nothing else changed). **Evidence:** new `test_hitl_report_bundle` **14/14** and `test_hitl_observation_wait` **7/7**, `test_hitl_import_gate` **5/5** (3 new), `test_accepted_sequence` **97/97** (4 new: a sealed pass, an `UNKNOWN` check refusing a success claim, a pass without a proven drain refused, a setup failure keeping its own verdict), `test_run_metadata` **6/6** (unchanged contract after the extraction), and the neighbouring suites green together; **six mutations** red-proved with every file restored byte-identically. **2026-09-30 — `response-driven-hitl-acceptance` task 3.2 closed: an abandoned managed run can no longer press, leaves no note sounding, and still drains before the capture is released (host tooling; no firmware, no build, no device action).** The watchdog bounded a *run*, but not the scenario inside it: on a ceiling breach `_run_with_watchdog` returned, its caller's context released the capture child, and the scenario thread kept working the wire with the serial port being torn down underneath it. `scripts/hitl/actions/cancellation.py` now owns the three properties. **Nothing is pressed after the abort**: every test edge goes through one `GuardedMidiOut`, which refuses to send once the run is cancelled, counts the refusal and raises `RunCancelled` (so the scenario *leaves* instead of computing on); `cancellable_sleep` bounds the time between two sends. **Held notes are released**: a run stopped between a `note_on` and its `note_off` leaves the device sounding a note, so the guard remembers what it put down and releases it — one `note_off` per held note plus `All Sound Off`/`All Notes Off` per channel it touched — and the release is idempotent. **The teardown is not a test gesture**: stopping the transport and draining must still happen, so it runs in an explicitly permitted phase (`teardown_call`) whose edges are counted apart, which is what lets a report say that nothing but teardown went out after the cancel. Cancellation is cooperative and observable (`CancelScope.check` with a first-reason-wins scope, `wait_for(cancel=…)`, `begin_run`/`active_cancel_scope`/`cancel_active_run` so the watchdog can reach a scope the driver owns), and `GuardedMidiOut.run()` is the outer context a driver adopts around its `DeviceSession` — absorb the cancel, release, record, unregister — with the drain still inner, so both drivers adopted it without re-indenting a body. **Ordering, which is the point:** `_run_with_watchdog` now cancels the registered run, waits a bounded grace (`HITL_CANCEL_GRACE_S`, default 30 s) for it to leave the wire, reports whether it stopped, and only then returns — the capture child is released after that; with no run registered there is nothing to cancel, so the earlier immediate release is kept and a scenario that ignores cancellation is abandoned with a named warning. **Both drivers** register the run, open through the guard, keep their shutdown inner, make their waits cancel-aware (raising the run's own reason rather than reporting a false "no receipt") and write `result = "CANCELLED"` + `cancel_reason` + the guard's own `midi` record into the same partial report they write on every other exit (nonzero). **Evidence:** new `scripts/test_hitl_cancellation.py` **21/21**, `test_managed_capture` **13/13** (the watchdog cancels a registered run, joins the scenario's own stop before returning, refuses the post-cancel send and releases exactly the held note), `test_accepted_sequence` **93/93** (a cancelled run writes `CANCELLED`, puts no further test edge on the wire except the release, still drains, and releases the capture after the shutdown), `test_retention_handoff_plan` **33/33**, neighbouring suites together — **405 tests / 15 suites**; **seven mutations** red-proved and every file restored byte-identically. Open in this section: 3.3 (managed metadata path, immutable versioned report schema, verify-only replay, the narrow observation-wait facade). [CANCELLATION-EXECUTION.md](../../openspec/changes/response-driven-hitl-acceptance/CANCELLATION-EXECUTION.md).
