**Stage changes shipped:**  
- `applyPendingHideAndShortenToNotes` now applies `Shorten`/`Hide` transforms by rebuilding the note vector once, avoiding repeated in-place erase scans for each pending change.  
- `saveNoteEditPass` gained `deferDerivedInvalidate` for batch callsites.  
- `sealPendingNoteChangesToEditPasses` now defers derived invalidation during companion row inserts and performs a single `playbackRevision` + `notifyCommittedContentChanged` publish after the batch.
- Companion sealing now performs one heap-reserve admission check for the entire companion batch and skips repeated per-row heap checks once the batch is admitted.
- Companion sealing now reserves `passes.editPasses` capacity for the full companion batch before row insertion, removing vector growth churn from the stop path.
- Added one batch timing line per companion seal (`DIAG,seal_companion_batch`) so each stop cycle records rows/sealed/duration directly.
- Added Tier-A stop sub-stage timing lines (`DIAG,odub_stop`) for `companion_seal`, `undo_push`, `mark_range`, `publish_prepared`, and `persist_request` inside `finalizeCommitSideEffects`, so long-tail stop cycles can be attributed to one owner step even under ring pressure.
- Companion per-row telemetry is now capped (first 8 `DIAG,seal_companion` rows) to avoid line-format/append churn during heavy stop cycles while preserving batch-level timing visibility (`DIAG,seal_companion_batch`).
- `markAffectedDisplayCacheRanges` now marks companion row spans first, then does one note-cache pass against the companion target-note set, instead of scanning `visualCache.notes` once per companion row.
- `applyPendingNoteChangesToOverdubSourceView` Add-note merge batching is restored (user-directed) so pending Add notes are merged in one pass before `Shorten`/`Hide` projection updates.
- `applyPendingHideAndShortenToNotes` now keeps Shorten/Hide transforms sorted by `noteId` and uses bounded lookup, removing repeated linear transform scans from the overdub-stop seal path while preserving Shorten/Hide outcomes.
- Added `SESSION_CAPTURE`-gated stop publish telemetry for the previously uninstrumented overdub-stop publish owner (`Loop::commitPendingCapturePass`) with cold/Flash placement (`LOOP_COLD_MEM`): `seal_fx_publish_pending_pass`, `seal_publish_promote_pass`, `seal_publish_span_cache_restamp`, `seal_publish_finalize_state`, `seal_publish_clear_capture`.
- `commitPendingCapturePass` span-cache restamp now hard-bounds stop-path work: when the committed pass exceeds the stop restamp event budget (`2048` events), restamp is deferred (`seal_publish_span_cache_restamp=deferred_event_budget`) and revision restamp is skipped so heavy rebuild work moves out of the synchronous stop envelope.
- `commitPendingCapturePass` now skips full committed-pass note reconstruction when no `NoteOn` id is missing from the span cache, and reconstructs only when missing ids remain after fast eligibility filtering.
- `mergeDisplayNotesIntoOverdubSourceView` and overdub-source span-cache add paths now use sorted `NoteId` indices for bounded membership checks instead of repeated per-candidate linear scans.
- Added one-shot post-stop causality probe lines: `ODUB,stop,debt_handoff` plus `DIAG,odub_debt` on the first PLAYING idle-maintenance turn after overdub stop, classifying visual/save debt as `pre_existing_debt`, `stop_created_debt`, `stop_amplified_debt`, or `newly_scheduled_after_stop` using pre-stop vs post-stop dirty/pending snapshots.
- Causality capture [`224752`](../../captures/session_20260820_224752.log) confirms stop-created visual debt in the first PLAYING maintenance turn (`ODUB,stop,debt_handoff=stop_created_debt`, 10/10 stops). Follow-up scheduling trim: while `playingMidiDrainAfterOverdubStopActive()` is true, idle visual cache slices are capped to 1 bar and mixed-dirty long-loop fallback stays neighborhood-bounded (no `UINT32_MAX` distance override in that drain window).
- Drain-window clamp now applies to all tracks in the same loop turn (via `main()` `postOverdubPlayingMidiDrain` -> `Track::processDeferredIdleMaintenance(..., postOverdubDrainWindowActive)`), so non-owner tracks cannot run broader PLAYING idle visual slices while a post-overdub drain window is active.
- Drain-window policy now restricts PLAYING idle visual maintenance to the overdub-stop owner track while the post-overdub drain window is armed; non-owner tracks defer their visual idle slices until the owner drain window clears, preventing unrelated pre-existing debt from consuming the same first post-stop MIDI turn.
- Behavior scope guard: this drain-window policy is stop-only. It is armed by `stopOverdubbing` (`armPlayingMidiDrainAfterOverdubStop`) and reset by `startOverdubbing`; the clamp gate applies only to PLAYING/STOPPED_RECORDING maintenance. OVERDUBBING and overdub-wrap commit paths keep normal note-update processing (`commitOverdubWrapAtSessionStart` still seals companions with source-view update enabled).
- Added post-stop arbitration gate in `main()` via `MidiServiceDrain::allowDeferredSave`: while the post-overdub drain window is active and deferred save work is pending, `StorageManager::processDeferredSaveState` is deferred for that loop turn so `idle_maint` and `persist_save` do not stack in the same drain-window slot.
- Added post-stop visual slice append guard in `Track::processDeferredIdleMaintenance`: for the full post-overdub drain window, `Loop::rebuildVisualCacheIdleSlice` runs without wrap-pair append (`allowOverdubWrapAppend=false`) so expensive `idle_append` work does not stack into stressed post-stop runtime windows.
- Added constrained fallback gather mode for the full post-overdub drain window: `Loop::rebuildVisualCacheIdleSlice(..., constrainFallbackGather=true)` removes pad bars and skips active edit-row projection in fallback gather windows, so post-stop fallback slices stay bounded when prepared windows are unavailable.
- Added no-progress constrained-slice backoff in `Track::processDeferredIdleMaintenance`: when a constrained fallback slice does not reduce dirty bars, the next constrained slice is deferred for `250 ms` (`overdubDrainFallbackRetryAtMs_`) to prevent repeated high-cost fallback churn in adjacent loop turns.
- Added non-overdub STOPPED follow-up optimization in `StorageManagerInternal::enqueueRemainingLoopSlotRestores`: boot background-fill now reuses boot-scanned in-RAM slot payload flags and skips per-slot SD reprobe during full enqueue, removing one-turn `SD.exists`/token-scan churn from `boot_commit`/`load_frame`.
- Further optimized `enqueueRemainingLoopSlotRestores` bulk admission: per-entry priority computation and per-entry queue sort are now deferred during full boot enqueue, then applied once via final `reprioritizeDeferredLoopSlotRestoreEntries()`, reducing boot-commit scheduler churn without changing restore ordering semantics.
- `enqueueRemainingLoopSlotRestores` now admits background-fill queue entries incrementally across loop turns (`kBootAdmissionEntriesPerTurn=4`) and only finalizes reprioritize/sort after admission completes, so STOPPED boot does not pay full remaining-slot admission in one `boot_commit` / `load_frame` window.
- Background `LoadLoopJob` stepping now enforces a transport-clock-safe resume policy: Low (non-focus) load jobs are disallowed while global transport clock is running and are parked/deferred for retry later, so slot-load catch-up cannot compete with active MIDI timing service.
- STOPPED deferred-maintenance scheduling now uses cancel/resume policy in `main()`: when all tracks are STOPPED, run `Track::processDeferredIdleMaintenance` for one track per turn (round-robin), and skip STOPPED maintenance entirely while global transport clock is running.
- Realtime visual-cache slices now defer wrap-pair append (`idle_append`) while playback/capture states are active; deferred append is resumed in STOPPED idle (`Loop::applyDeferredVisualCacheWrapAppend`) so MIDI service keeps priority during PLAYING/OVERDUBBING while append work restarts later.
- Realtime visual-cache gather restart cooldown (`activeVisualSliceRetryAtMs_`) was rolled back after reboot evidence in [`012714`](../../captures/session_20260821_012714.log) to remove the newest strict throttle while retaining append defer/resume and post-overdub drain-window guards.

### Overdub-start begin-capture long-delay restoration — validated

**Evidence:** [`165534`](../../captures/session_20260820_165534.log), [`165956`](../../captures/session_20260820_165956.log)

**Owner:** `Loop::rebuildOverdubSourceSpanCache`, `Track::startOverdubbing` (`ODUB,stage,begin_capture`).

**Invariant:** Overdub start stays deterministic while an overdub session is active: if prepared spans are unavailable, start/wrap does not force a full-loop materialize on the timing-critical path.

**Root cause proved in captures:** `ODUB,stage,begin_capture` spiked to about **2.2 s** (`2194189 us`, `2248843 us`) in [`165956`](../../captures/session_20260820_165956.log), and `Live Overdub -> Overdubbing started` was delayed by **2143-2249 ms** on early starts. The same pattern appears in [`165534`](../../captures/session_20260820_165534.log) (~2102/2189 ms). This directly maps to `rebuildOverdubSourceSpanCache` falling back to `passes.materializeToEventVector` when prepared spans are unavailable.

**Stage change shipped:** Restored overdub-session cache fallback in `rebuildOverdubSourceSpanCache`: when prepared spans are unavailable during an active overdub session, reuse prior cache notes instead of forcing full-loop materialization on start/wrap. Non-session behavior remains unchanged (full materialize is still allowed outside active overdub sessions).

**Status:** Native **1397/1397**. `teensy41-capture-serial` build **PASS**. New baseline [`210319`](../../captures/session_20260820_210319.log): `ODUB,stage,begin_capture` stays bounded at **1851-6443 us** (median **2070 us**), confirming start stalls are no longer the active bottleneck.

**Historical outlier context:** [`170724`](../../captures/session_20260820_170724.log) contains a one-cycle stop-path outlier (`ODUB,stop,seal=310980 us`, `display=320406 us`). The new planning baseline is [`210319`](../../captures/session_20260820_210319.log) runtime windows above (published stop display 56.451-71.803 ms; first post-stop MIDI Input Gap 78.634-145.373 ms).

### Overdub-start reboot — reverted to baseline, blocked on instrumentation

**Evidence:** [`162146`](../../captures/session_20260820_162146.log), [`132145`](../../captures/session_20260820_132145.log), [`143518`](../../captures/session_20260820_143518.log)

**Owner:** `Track::startOverdubbing`, `TrackManager::startOverdubbingTrack`, `DebugSessionCapture` capture ring.

**Symptom:** USB drops immediately after `[TRACK] Overdubbing started @ tick N`, the final statement of `Track::startOverdubbing`. Reproduces on first and second overdub start.

**Not caused by the 2026-08-20 removals.** The reboot is present in [`132145`](../../captures/session_20260820_132145.log) and [`143518`](../../captures/session_20260820_143518.log), before any of them. Commits `4af158a`, `39b8e1d`, `983262d`, `98699b6`, `6ff4142` are reverted; the tree is byte-identical to `28cf6e3`. Pass accumulation is also ruled out — the first capture of the day already reached `pass,99` and the last reached `pass,101`.

**Capture blind spot (why eight successive fixes all "made no difference"):** two independent mechanisms starve overdub telemetry out of the ring.

| Mechanism | Owner | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Flush budget `<= 8` takes the drop-only branch | `DebugSessionCapture::flushCaptureBuffer` | Discards up to 8 non-Tier-A head records and returns without transmitting. The overdub `SC_REC_FLUSH_PENDING_REVTS(8)` sites delete telemetry instead of sending it. |
| Tier-B append refused while ring is full and head is Tier-A | `DebugSessionCapture::appendCaptureRecord` | `ODUB,stage`, `MI`, `MO`, `LED` never enter the ring. `DIAG,lcr,` and `VCACHE,` are Tier-A per `CaptureLineTier::isTierALine`. |
| `formatPhaseLine` 1 s rate limit never engages | `LoopContentResolution` device-gate slice machine | `stepChanged` is true on every slice because the machine alternates `idx` ↔ `pair`, so the Tier-A `DIAG,lcr,phase` line emits per slice, not per second. |

In [`162146`](../../captures/session_20260820_162146.log) the last `#CAP,…,MI,…` is at 9.387 s and the last `LED` at 14.89 s, while `DIAG,lcr,phase` keeps emitting to 33.38 s (355 lines). The record button press at 35.198 s produced a text log line but **no** `MI` capture line, so Tier-B appends were already being refused when overdub started. `ODUB,stage,manager_enter` / `manager_done` are therefore absent for instrumentation reasons, not because that code did not run.

**Fault reason never observed.** `setup()` prints `CrashReport` before `logger.setup(LOG_DEBUG)`, and every reconnect boot in the 2026-08-20 captures begins at `Logger initialized with level: 3`. The pre-logger boot output is absent from all of them. The firmware also writes `CrashReport` to `crashlog.txt` on SD (`main.cpp` `setup()`); that file is the authoritative record and has not been read.

**Next:** read SD `crashlog.txt` to classify the fault (allocator abort vs hard fault vs watchdog) before any further code change. Do not attribute the reboot to a removal again without an `ODUB,stage` line or a crash record.

**Status:** Native **1397/1397**. `teensy41-capture-serial` RAM1 code **424572** / locals **4768**. Not flashed.

### Consume candidate attribution — Stage 1A/1B COMPLETE (observability only, superseded)

**Plan:** [`overdub_consume_ledger_merge_enhancement.md`](../Plans/overdub_consume_ledger_merge_enhancement.md)

**Owner:** `Loop::accumulatePendingNoteChangesForIncomingNote`. Selection behavior **unchanged** — this does **not** start the parked consume merge.

**Invariant:** consume candidate selection is measured, not changed: every candidate is attributed to the occupy-id lookup, the window scan, or late JIT materialization.

**Status:** Counters + `DIAG,consume,select` shipped. **1B detail diagnostics shipped:** `DIAG,consume,norowid` (ids that failed to resolve to a source-view row) and `DIAG,consume,scanadd` (scan-added candidate ids with `in_ids=0|1`). **Consume merge selection change REJECTED** — HITL [`191133`](../../captures/session_20260819_191133.log): 3 of 5 attributed holds had a **non-empty** occupy set where the window scan was the only path to a participant (2× `idsel=1`, 1× `norow=1`). Follow-up HITL [`193024`](../../captures/session_20260819_193024.log): `norow` did not reproduce (`norow=0`, `norowid=0`), while `scanadd` persisted (18 lines, all `in_ids=0`). Empty-ids fallback remains load-bearing. Native **1386/1386**. RAM1 code **425964** / locals **4768**.

**Stage 1A guard check:** `overlapNoteIds` is written by `snapshotOverlapHoldCandidates` (open at `holdStart`) **and** `collectOverlapHoldPlaybackNoteOn` (NoteOns during the hold, from `sendMidiEvent` before the `playbackEmitMidiOutput_` gate). `appendNotesForIds` cannot reach a note absent from `overdubSourceViewNotes_`, so the long-loop JIT branch is the only path to a JIT-merged ahead note — proven by `test_consume_attribution_counts_late_note_for_jit_ahead_candidate`. Blocking additive candidates on non-empty ids therefore changes long-loop consume, which a 1-bar gate cannot observe.

**Long-loop JIT class did not reproduce:** `why=hold` **140** with long loops present (`live=18432`, `live=52224`), yet every line is `jit=0` / `late=0`. Reachable in native, not the device problem.

**Closed 2026-08-19.** Stage 1A delivered its purpose: the attribution evidence decided the selection question. **RC-L3 (shipped, HITL verify open) — stored-MIDI verification off the stop path:** `emitStoredMidiVerification` ran inside MIDI button dispatch at overdub stop and cost 342.7 ms / 325.5 ms in [`013917`](../../captures/session_20260813_013917.log) (flush itself under 1 ms): a full `mergeActiveCapturePasses`, one `SEVT` line per note event over 3554 events, the capped wrap-pair scan, then a second full `reconstructNotes` for at most 32 `DNTE` lines. The ring overflowed at both stops, so most `SEVT` lines were dropped and the `seal` / `finalize` / `set_state` stage lines were evicted with them. Now `queueDeferredStoredMidiVerification` only sets a flag; `processDeferredStoredMidiVerification` drains from `processDeferredIdleMaintenance` in 64-event slices (16 while `hasDeferredSaveWork`), flattening once on the first slice and phasing notes → wrap pairs → display notes. Functions are `TRACK_COLD_MEM` — in ITCM they pushed RAM1 past a 32 KB block boundary.

**RC-L3b (shipped, device verify open) — one-shot + idle-only drain:** deferring during PLAYING still blocked MIDI for seconds because the first slice does a full merge ([`020631`](../../captures/session_20260813_020631.log) `msi` 2.95 s). Verification is now **one overdub stop per boot** (`#CAP,DIAG,stored_verify,armed,0` when disarmed; reboot to re-arm for another HITL evidence run). Drain runs only when transport is fully idle (same gate as REVT), not during PLAYING/OVERDUB. Second+ overdub stops in the same session skip verification so manual retests are not penalized.

- **RC-S0a** `isTierATextLine` skipped two commas, so Tier-A classification was inert and the ring evicted every DIAG window. Parse extracted to `CaptureLineTier::isTierALine` (`test_capture_line_tier` PASS); Tier-A may now only be displaced by Tier-A.
- **RC-S0b** `MemoryMonitor::logStatus()` external-pool walk blocked the loop **593 ms** and lost external MIDI clock. Walk is now `setup()`-only (`logStatus(true)`); runtime reports `pool_size` (O(1)). Guide exemption removed.

**S0 run [`145555`](../../captures/session_20260812_145555.log):** DIAG timing windows survive through RECORD + both overdubs. `midisvc` 0.9–1.1 ms during RECORD vs **129–149 ms** during PLAYING/OVERDUB (762.5 ms at overdub entry), against `clk`/`tracks` ≤ 8.83 ms — `handleMidiInput()` duration is the dominant term and clock dispatch is not. **RC-S0c:** windows before 177 s were lost because `flushCaptureBuffer` never transmits Tier-A under the timing-critical budget; fix is a bounded Tier-A transmit allowance (roadmap O2 / [investigation §31b](../Plans/archive/refinements/runtime_scheduling_timing_envelope_investigation.md#31b-s0-run-145555--first-capture-phase-envelope)).

Transition feel is the Clock dispatch reorder (Clock no longer transport-first).

**2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.12a: the admission limit on the decided accounting unit (DEC-108 §14) — the task stays open.** `WindowAdmissionAccounting` (in `RuntimePlaybackViewConfig`) accounts the capture interval's **effective** events plus **outstanding reservations** plus the **closure reserve inside L**, with `fits(...)` as the one predicate, an `admit(...)` that returns a **named** `Outcome` and never half-accepts, and per-bar/span bounds that are **conservative and clamped by L**. Two invariants are pinned by `static_assert` where they cannot drift: `kWindowAdmissionLimit == kEventsPerView` (**L is the window's storage capacity** — no partition multiplier) and `kWindowClosureReserve < L` (the reserve is inside the limit; its value 128 is a **declared provisional** figure, not a measurement). Interaction acceptance is structurally outside the limit: the counters hold content only, so a stop/switch/undo request has no representation to be refused by (DEC-078's separation upheld by construction). Verification: focused **56/56**, full native **2687 / 2680 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, `teensy41-capture-serial` **SUCCESS** on a clean rebuild with `variables 96,192` **unchanged** / `code 391,928 + padding 1,288` (448 B headroom) and **no re-base**; two mutations red-proved with byte-identical restores (the reserve moved outside L; the per-bar bound not clamped). **OWED in 3.12:** the **bounded legacy paged path** (fixed-capacity immutable pages with a resumable cursor preserving revision, ordering and exactly-once emission — fixture 5.5) and the **MIDI-edge wiring** of the limit into capture acceptance, without which "capacity pressure is refused before acceptance" is a property of the unit rather than of the running system. **2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 4.3: the served window's stream is readable, and content parity across a window boundary is proven natively (F-7); the task stays open on its device leg and on the obligation the measurement names.** `Track::playbackWindowEventAtForSlot(slot, cursor, out)` is the **ordered event stream the served window holds**, rendered exactly as the emission path renders it (`storage.events[storage.order[cursor]]`) — read-only, O(1), allocation-free, no new state, and it reads the window that is **served** (complete, published, valid interval), never a prepared successor. **The gap was verified rather than assumed:** the lane exposed identity, coverage, a count and a presence predicate and **no way to read what a window holds**; nothing in production consumes a window's events (the emission path still reads bridge/pair/oracle/merged, and `stepPlaybackViewMaintenance` returns `Idle` in production because nothing requests a window — `ExecutionBounds.md` row 27 still denies active windowed playback), and no native fixture read a built window's content, so the spec's parity clause had no observable on this side at all. **The proof:** 32 successive windows over a 64-bar demoted loop (two-bar centred intervals, so the request sample tiles exactly), each built to completion, each served interval asserted against `playbackWindowInterval`, each read through the new accessor, concatenated and compared **row for row** (tick, type, channel, note) with the whole-loop stream from the project's **existing** resolver (`LoopContentResolution::resolveWindow(root, 0, loopLength)` — the primitive the content-verification pipeline's `effective` dump is built on, not a second pipeline): nothing lost, duplicated or reordered across all 31 boundaries. The **closure** case is measured, not assumed: the boundary note's ON is served by tile 0 and its OFF by tile 1 — the lane does **not** synthesize a closure at the edge — so the concatenation balances (no note-on left unclosed by the transition) while either window alone does not; the transition's closure is therefore the **consumer's** obligation (3.7's emission switch with 4.5's ledger set). Also measured and owed to 3.7: the policy is *centred*, so consecutive requests at arbitrary phases **overlap**, and a consumer must not double-serve the overlap. Both publication paths are pinned as measured: the **first** window installs as the served one, every **replacement** publishes as the ready successor and the consumer-side edge adopts it. *Verification:* focused `test_runtime_working_set_ownership` **66/66** (+1 fixture), `test_storage_loop_io` **52/52**, `test_playback_prewarm` **190/190** (the cited pin), `test_midi_service_drain` **38/38**; full native **2698 / 2691 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**; `teensy41-capture-serial` **SUCCESS** on a true clean rebuild (82.4 s) with `variables 96,192` **unchanged** / `code 392,328 + padding 888` (48 B above the floor), byte-identical to the eight previous slices. Four mutations red-proved, each at a named file with its anchor count asserted and each restored byte-identically (the policy's centring, the window span, reading the ready successor instead of the served window, and the accessor's bounds) — **with their bound stated:** mutations that break the lane's output are caught by the fixture's interval/coverage pins *before* the row comparison runs, so that comparison is the claim those pins protect rather than a separately red-proved assertion. **Not claimed:** no production consumer; **no device/HITL evidence** (the spec's pipeline is the HITL content verification, whose windowed profile is 6.4 and whose device legs are 6.5); loop-wrap content is deliberately not exercised here; **4.3 stays open** on its device leg, the closure obligation at the transition (3.7 with 4.5) and the overlap rule (3.7). **2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, first increment: fair, bounded, deadline-ordered service at the **holder level** (DEC-108 §13b); the task stays open on the wiring and on the starvation/envelope halves.** The owner rotation already existed *and was already proved* (the unconditional 7-owner cycle, with `test_select_deferred_idle_owner_backlog_snapshot_two_of_eight` asserting one turn per owner per cycle); what did not exist is the level below it — which **holder** (one slot's owed build) an admitted `PlaybackViewMaintenance` turn serves. There the scan was ascending first-match with **no cursor**, and **no deadline was stored at all**: `beginCoverageBuild` takes `handoffPhase` and drops it, so "earliest outstanding playback deadline" had no value to order by. `include/Utils/MidiServiceDrain.h` now carries the pure `selectPlaybackHolder(cursor, holders, count, out)` with `PlaybackHolder` (eligible / can progress / outstanding deadline), `PlaybackHolderCursor` and the named `PlaybackHolderSelection { None, Service, AllBlocked }` — header-only, no allocation, and **no new state**: the deadline is the phase at which the playhead next enters the interval the build serves, the figure `Track::requestPlaybackWindow` already passes as `handoffPhase`. **Proved as five bounds:** each able holder is served exactly once per rotation and the next rotation continues from the cursor; the earliest outstanding deadline is served first (deadlines deliberately in the reverse of the holder order, so an ascending scan answers wrongly); a holder with a deadline outranks one without, while deadline-less holders still rotate evenly; a **blocked holder is never chosen**, the others keep the bound, and it is served within one rotation of becoming able — skipped over, never lost; and "nothing owed" (`None`) is distinct from "all owed and blocked" (`AllBlocked`), with `kNoPlaybackHolder` in every non-serving outcome and the rotation advancing in both (never a latch). **2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 6: the starvation half, the composed progress bound, and a measured contradiction in the declared envelope (DEC-108 §13b / task 3.10).** Test-only (no production line changed). This supplies the task's own verification sentence — the **production selector** composed with the lane's own turn while the lane owes two windows — asserting that **every one of the seven deferred-idle owners, the lane included, is served exactly once per rotation** (no starvation, no extra share), that the lane progresses to completion with one completion per owed window, and pinning the measured turn count. **Not re-claimed:** the exact rotation was already proved *including* the lane (RWO's `test_select_deferred_idle_owner_backlog_snapshot_two_of_eight`), the lane's one-grain-per-call by 3.1's `expectedTurns == 5`, and the blocked-holder case by increment 1; the lane is **never denied** its turn (`deferredIdleOwnerDependsOnVisualCacheWrap` covers only `VisualCache`/`LoadAndDisplay`), and the caller's single-dispatch shape (`SlotProvision` and the lane served before the transport guards, each branch ending in `return`) is **build-verified** because `src/main.cpp` is not native-linkable. **The finding, measured and numeric:** for one 64-bar loop and two owed windows carrying **81 notes**, the lane needed **58 grains and 60 lane turns** with 2 completions, while the contract it is admitted under declares `3 + 3 + 1 = 7` grains at quanta 64/48 with a 3-denied-turn allowance → **28 turns** worst case. So **the declaration does not bound this work shape**, and two of its own numbers disagree by roughly an order of magnitude: `3` order grains × `48` = **144 ordered entries**, against a window declared to hold `kEventsPerView = 2048`. In the contract's own currency: the admission (`canCompleteBeforeHandoff`) judges the handoff lead with the **declared** grains — the 29-bar / 22 272-tick lead the family already uses, and 4.4's derived 30-bar floor — while a shape needing 60 lane turns needs `60 × 768 ≈ 60 bars`, so such a shape can be **admitted and still miss its handoff**; the one-pass-late rule is the designed answer to the miss, but the *declared* envelope is unsupported for the shape. **The derivation is not invented here** — assertion (C) deliberately pins the *violation*, so deriving the envelope properly inverts it and forces the record to be updated. *Red-proofs* (anchors with occurrence count asserted = 1; byte-identical restores, drain sha256 `1c019eb0…b5c913`, build sha256 `d79ad359…c5674c7`): **M95** an extra lane turn per rotation → `Expected 60 Was 1` (the priority hack starves one owner to a single turn — exactly the property); **M96** the fill grain serving twice the declared quantum → `Expected 60 Was 59` (and 3.1's grain fixture and 3.2's publication fixture with it); **M97** a lane turn skipped every other turn → 18 cases fail. *Verification:* `test_runtime_working_set_ownership` **71/71** (+1 fixture); full native **2706 / 2699 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**; build **SUCCESS** in **2.77 s** — a **relink, not a rebuild** (no production line changed), RAM1 line **byte-identical** (`variables 96,192 / code 392,328 + padding 888`, 48 B headroom), **no re-base**. **Task 3.10 stays open** on the **envelope derivation** (now a concrete measured problem, not a note), the **wiring** (still no production caller), and the systematic **grain-cost sweep** (this is one shape; how fill and order costs scale is not established). The **starvation half is closed at the allocation level**; what each owner does inside its turn stays the caller's, build-verified. Evidence: [`evidence/2026-10-02-s310f-composed-service-bound/EVIDENCE.md`](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-02-s310f-composed-service-bound/EVIDENCE.md).

**2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 7: the measured grain-cost model and the supported window derived from it (DEC-108 §13b / task 3.10; test-only).** This is the increment increments 6 and 2 both pointed at — **derive the envelope from grain costs without inventing a microsecond budget** — and the envelope is now derived from a **measurement**. A sweep drives one owed window to completion, reading `nextCoverageBuildGrain()` **before** each turn so the fill/order split is the owner's own answer: window events **1 → 1 turn / 0 orders**, **10 → 1 / 0**, **20 → 11 orders / 12 turns**, **40 → 25 / 27**, **80 → 57 / 60**, **160 → 127 / 132**. Controls in the same run: **80 notes cost identically on a 32-bar and a 64-bar loop**, and the same 80 notes **spread across the loop** cost **one** turn — so the cost is a function of the **window's event count alone**, it has a **threshold near 10 events** (below which the build finishes in one grain with no order grain at all), and above it the order pass is **super-linear** (per-note cost 0.55 → 0.79 grains, doubling ratios ×2.27/×2.28/×2.23). **The derived bound, in the contract's own currency:** a lane turn advances the playhead at most `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn`, so a window's need is `turns × 768` ticks of playhead travel — 80 events = **46 080 ticks ≈ 60 bars** (fits a 64-bar loop, **not** a 32-bar one), 160 events = **101 376** (fits neither). **The contradictions, now numeric:** the declared `3 + 3 + 1 = 7` grains at quanta 64/48 (worst case 28 turns) covers roughly `N ≈ 5–10`, not a window of 80; an 80-event window on a **32-bar** loop was nevertheless **admitted** while needing 46 080 ticks, far beyond the declared **29-bar lead** the admission judged it by; and `kWindowAdmissionLimit = kEventsPerView = 2048` extrapolates to ~**1 600 lane turns ≈ 1 600 bars**, an order of magnitude beyond any admissible loop. **Preferred reconciliation, stated and deliberately NOT applied:** keep the grain quanta (a deliberate timing choice with a measurement behind it) and derive **both** the declared grain counts and 3.12's admitted window size from the measured envelope and the loop's own length — confidence **high** that the *capacity* is the wrong side to keep (three measurements agree), **medium** on the exact functional form (four points establish the shape, not the constant; the order pass's algorithm is not read here). It is not applied because it moves the declared lead, 3.12's admission limit and 4.4's derived floor, and would **refuse shapes admitted today** — a contract change with behavioural effect; assertion (D) is written as the *contradiction*, so applying it inverts it. *Red-proofs* (anchors with occurrence count asserted = 1; byte-identical restores, window-build TU sha256 `d79ad359…c5674c7`, view-build TU sha256 `c752601e…a31717`): **M98** the order quantum 48 → 96 → `Expected 11 Was 6` on the pinned table (and 3.1's and 3.2's fixtures); **M99** always entering the order phase → `Expected 1 Was 2` on the sparse-window assertion; **M100** the declared `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn` ×100 → the derivation's equality pin fails, i.e. **(D) reads the declared field, not a literal** (20 cases fail in total). *Verification:* `test_runtime_working_set_ownership` **72/72** (+1 fixture); full native **2707 / 2700 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**; build **SUCCESS** in 3.32 s — a **relink, not a rebuild** (test-only), RAM1 line **byte-identical**, **no re-base**. **Not claimed:** the model's constant is not derived; the reconciliation is proposed, not applied; the samples are one content shape; no device observation; the lane still has no production caller. **A fixture bug of mine, recorded:** the super-linearity assertion was first written backwards and the run caught it. Evidence: [`evidence/2026-10-02-s310g-cost-model/EVIDENCE.md`](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-02-s310g-cost-model/EVIDENCE.md).


**2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 8: source-lifetime repair, holder-fairness repair, and the derived admission (not enabled) (DEC-108 §13b / task 3.10).** This answers an independent review thread, and two of the three items were **defects in my own earlier increments**. **(1) Source lifetime.** `prepareOwingWindowHolder` gathered the request source into a **stack-local** `SessionMidiEventVec` while `RuntimePlaybackViewFill::step` reads `source_[cursor_]` **across turns** — so every turn after the helper returned read a dead frame. **The repair is what proves the review's point that this invalidated measurements: three fixtures' outcomes changed the moment the source became valid** (the composed fixture's completion count, the sparse window's 1 → 2 turns, and two cases of the urgency fixture turning out **unable to fail** — they passed only because the dangling source had made a slot stop owing — so they were removed, since an assertion that cannot fail is not evidence). The fix is a file-scope **per-slot** buffer: two slots can owe at once, and the caller owns the source for the build's whole duration. **(2) Holder fairness.** `selectPlaybackHolder` applied earliest-deadline-first **globally**, and my own doc even called that "the tighter of the two readings". The spec is explicit — *"Service SHALL **rotate round-robin across eligible holders**, and **within a holder** SHALL serve the earliest outstanding playback deadline first"*, with the scenario *"WHEN **a holder has more than one outstanding playback deadline**"* — and the design names the order: **"2 — Fairness, then deadline order."** The global form **starves**: a permanently-earlier deadline wins every rotation and the cursor cannot rescue the loser. Repair: **`selectPlaybackHolderRoundRobin`** is the across-holders rule, `selectPlaybackHolder` keeps the within-a-holder role with its doc corrected at the source, `src/main.cpp`'s track choice uses the round-robin form, and a new fixture drives the production composition with two tracks whose deadlines really are unequal and whose near obligation is long-lived (80 notes) — both are served within one rotation, where the old rule took every turn. **(3) The derived admission.** `applyWindowCostToContract` is now the single source of truth: `ceil(events / kPlaybackViewFillQuantum)` fills + `RuntimePlaybackOrderBuilder::requiredGrains(events, kPlaybackViewOrderQuantum)` order grains + one promotion grain. **The corrected cost model, measured with valid sources:** events = **2 × notes** (increment 7's column was notes), fills = **⌈events/64⌉ exactly**, and orders **equal the helper exactly where a merge runs** (11/25/57/127 for 40/80/160/320 events) while falling **below** it where the input is already ordered (20 events: bound 5, measured 1 — increment 7's "threshold near 10 events" was that skip, not a size threshold) — and increment 7's 2 048-event extrapolation (~1 600 grains) was simply wrong: the helper gives **982 order + 32 fill**. It is **implemented and deliberately NOT enabled**, for a measured reason: at the *declared* `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn` and the rotation-derived gap, an 80-note window's derived need is ≈ **428 bars**, so enabling it refuses the shapes the current constants admit — the capacity reduction the review said not to approve on unmeasured evidence. **The service-gap bound is split honestly:** the **rotation** half is proven (the exact rotation sequence, plus the new fairness fixture), while the **ticks-per-turn** half is not — `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn` remains the declared one bar, and the sweep fixture now asserts that as a statement so the envelope cannot be read as supported ("a supported deadline envelope still requires a proven service-gap bound — not merely larger constants"). *Verification:* `test_runtime_working_set_ownership` **73/73**; full native **2708 / 2701 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**; build **SUCCESS** from a **true rebuild** (82.6 s, cache cleared) with the RAM1 line **byte-identical** (`variables 96,192 / code 392,328 + padding 888`) and **no re-base**. Evidence: [`evidence/2026-10-02-s310h-lifetime-fairness-derivation/EVIDENCE.md`](../../openspec/changes/windowed-playback-generation/evidence/2026-10-02-s310h-lifetime-fairness-derivation/EVIDENCE.md).


**2026-10-02 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 9: the service-gap unit pinned, increment 8's bound retracted as non-general (DEC-108 §13b / task 3.10).** An independent review caught a real error in increment 8's record: the "≈428 bars" figure for an 80-note window was **wrong twice**. It **double-counted** the owner rotation, because `maximumPhaseAdvancePerTurn` is declared *per this owner's own opportunity* (a `PlaybackViewMaintenance` dispatch), which already contains the other six deferred owners' share; and it **omitted the contention inside the lane** — one *track* of every `H` eligible tracks per lane turn (`src/main.cpp`'s offer round-robin), plus the chosen track's sibling slots, whose earlier intervals may legitimately take that turn under the spec's within-holder earliest-deadline-first. So it was a single-track/single-slot figure presented as a general per-window bound. **Repair:** the field's **unit is pinned where it is declared**, together with what it does *not* contain and the statement that `canCompleteBeforeHandoff`'s `grains × (denied + 1)` is **not yet a complete bound**; the production contention offsets are named from the production shape (`kDeferredIdleOwnerCount × Config::NUM_TRACKS × Config::MAX_LOOPS_PER_TRACK`, with `main.cpp`'s 8-offer bound as the smaller divisor where it applies); and the sweep fixture now asserts the **structure** — the measured 61 grains for an 80-note window, the still-declared one-bar advance, and the admission's turn count being smaller than the contention factor — instead of a fabricated figure. **Consequence, recorded rather than papered over:** leaving cost enforcement disabled does **not** make the current admission safe, so active windowed playback stays **gated**, which is what `ExecutionBounds.md` row 27 already records and what 3.7's block depends on. **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 24: the retained pending preparation request (native verified; O8 deferred).** The item both landed packets owed — "`TrackInterferenceBudgetExceeded` is a named refusal and becomes a promise only when a caller keeps the pending request and its original deadline; no such caller or store exists yet" — is now in, and the task's soundness hole is closed: **a refused request is deferred, never dropped.** `PlaybackViewPendingRequest` + `PlaybackViewPendingReason` land as per-slot state on the externally allocated `LoopPlaybackRuntime` (no DTCM, no RAM1 `variables`): the source identity, the coverage interval, the **absolute deadline with its clock epoch and loop geometry**, the origin phase and the bounded cost an admitted window would carry. Retention fires at the four "not now" refusals (`BuildInFlight`, `SuccessorAlreadyPrepared`, `TrackInterferenceBudgetExceeded`, `CannotCompleteBeforeHandoff`); the admission that accepts the demand **discharges it whole**; `ContractUndeclared`, `AdmissionRefused`, `NotServable`, `SourceUnavailable`, `SourceNotCurrent`, `WindowExceedsRetainedCapacity` and `NoRuntime` retain nothing, so retention is per refusal name rather than a blanket. **Coalescing** (DEC-108 §13(a)) keeps the **oldest outstanding deadline as one coherent position** — deadline, epoch, geometry, origin phase and origin stamp all from the promise it names — while the content (identity, interval, cost) follows the newest attempt, since a newer window may satisfy the older obligation; an unqualified re-attempt never overwrites a qualified demand. An epoch or geometry change **voids the position and never the obligation** (§13(c)) and is named by the reader; identity is **generation-qualified** (§13(d)) so a returning slot never revives an earlier operation, and a demand under the new generation starts a fresh record rather than inheriting the older deadline. A pending demand is deliberately **not** outstanding work, so the per-track budget does not charge a sibling for it. **Fixtures (5)**: retained-with-original-deadline + discharged-by-admission + the nothing-owed class; the demand owes no grain; coalescing keeps the oldest deadline; epoch/geometry invalidation; the generation change. **Red-proofs M120–M126**, each failing its own named assertion and restored byte-identically (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp e98595129187ceee`, `TrackPlaybackRuntime.cpp 35eec9683a0fdfd2`, `TrackPlaybackRuntime.h 2e50b234a0cce56c`). **Defects found by running it, mine and fixed:** the first `retainViewPendingRequest` read the retained record through an alias **after** replacing it, handing the coalesced promise the newest attempt's origin stamp with the oldest deadline (the O4 fixture caught the incoherence; every retained field is now read into a locals set first); a fixture precondition of mine asserted nothing; and the **host-ABI size pin was unreachable dead code** — it sat in the `#else` of a branch whose `#if` already required `__IMXRT1062__`, so the "host pin unchanged at 6,544" claims of earlier records described an assertion no compiler evaluated (measured on the clean previous tree the host object is **8,624 B**); it is live (native) from this slice and re-based on measurement. Activation therefore needs the **clock-owner wiring**, not a better constant; the switch stays off, the enforced path stays exercised by the fixtures that enable it, and activation is recorded as the step-4 remainder with its cause. **Seven re-bases are recorded rather than smoothed** (the declaration mirroring constants 768 -> 16 and 3 -> `NUM_TRACKS - 1`; the declares-caps / one-grain / atomic-publication / grain-cost fixtures computing their request lead from the contract's own derivation over their own source; the service-gap fixture's wall-clock absolutes 2 000/1 000 ms -> 41/20 ms; **monotone request stamps** in the shared helpers because the budget refuses a clock that goes backwards — which is what the "farther holder first, nearer holder second" fixtures were doing — with the deadline-clock and budget fixtures reading their reference tick from the admitted record; and shape moves *inside* the declared envelope: 40 -> 200 bars for the two-holder fixtures, the increment-24 retention fixtures to 30 bars, the charge fixture to 4/20 bars so the H-factor decides, the refusals-by-name fixture from 900 to 30 bars). No fixture was re-based to hide a capacity change. Verified: focused **90/90** (+1 fixture pinning the terms, the derivation and the capability), full native **2,733 / 2,726 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, build **SUCCESS**, RAM1 line **byte-identical** (`variables 96,192`, code 390,472 + padding 2,744; no size-pin movement — this increment changes constants, the lead-side accounting and comments), `git diff --check` clean, `openspec validate --strict` valid. **Mutations:** **M127** the per-turn term back to the placeholder bar fails the envelope fixture (*"and it is the stated margin over the measured per-opportunity advance"*, `Expected 16 Was 768`) and 23 fixtures in total; **M128** the lead judged on the declared basis counts fails the charge and declares-caps boundary fixtures; **M129** the denial allowance back to 3 fails the envelope fixture (*"the denial allowance is the across-track rotation (H - 1), not an invented 3"*) and the H-factor fixture — all restored byte-identically (`include/Track.h 5c4a5b0121796179`, `src/Track/TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp f653a2d6559ac744`). No upload, no HITL, no timing-envelope claim. **Owed:** activation (the callers' qualified clock stamps), increment 24's re-attempt (O8), a production requester of committed windows (qualification blocker 1), the owner's confirmation of the declared `Delta-max`, the `H x K` sweep and the device leg. **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 25b: the declared `Delta-max` set from the device leg — and the provisional value falsified by it.** The owner asked for the number to be *proved on the card first* rather than derived from a margin, and the proof did its job: the provisional **16 ticks** (2x the measured p50) was **refused by the measurement**. Two managed baseline runs of the **authoritative entry point** (`scripts/host_midi_hitl.py run --preset base --track 8 --loop-slot 4 --midi-channel 8`, canonical `STIM-BASE-2-2-01@v1` unchanged; internal clock, then host clock at 300 BPM with `--boot-reset`; 68 352 and 5 888 lane opportunities) measured the quantity the field actually bounds — the advance across a turn **whose predecessor was eligible** (`DIAG,win_gap`'s `eligiblePredecessorMax`, which the schema-2 sampler separates from idle intervals) — at **internal: p50 0 / p90 9 / p99 15 / max 17** and **300 BPM: p50 8 / p90 16 / p99 48 / max 48**. Two internal rows and six 300-BPM rows exceeded 16, so the declaration moves to **64 ticks**: at or above both measured maxima with a stated margin (1.33x the worst, at the fastest declared tempo where 64 ticks is 66.7 ms; 3.8x the internal maximum). The envelope fixture's pin changed from a margin over the median to **measured** pins (declared ≥ 48, ≤ 4/3 of it, and ≥ the internal 17) — which is the pin that caught the provisional value, and M127 confirms it still catches the placeholder. **Starvation did not appear in either leg** (0 saturated gaps; the largest *all-dispatch* gap, 366 ticks, had an **ineligible** predecessor, i.e. it was idle time, not a lost opportunity), which is the strongest evidence yet for increment 17's split: the seconds-scale episodes belong to the lag rule's overrun policy, and a bound on one turn cannot hold a run of *lost* turns. **Image honesty:** both legs ran the **flashed** image `7c2a1377…` (the tree at `4a7cef70`), *not* this increment's tree — the measured path (lane dispatcher `src/main.cpp`, sampler `PlaybackLaneMeasurement.h`, row emitter `DebugSessionCapture.*`) is byte-identical in both (verified by diff), no production path requests a window so the admission is never called in this flow, and **no upload was performed**. Leg A's baseline verdict was FAIL on the large-loop bounds verifier's 100 ms slice declaration (max 104 640 us — a pre-existing verdict issue on that image) and leg B's was PASS; the lane measurement does not depend on either. **Capability consequence, stated:** one 63-entry window charged with one same-track sibling needs **11 008 ticks ≈ 14.3 bars** of lead under this declaration (3 328 ≈ 4.3 bars at 16; 123 648 ≈ 161 bars under the placeholder), and a 160-note/320-event window needs ~90 bars on its own. **Re-bases this correction required, all recorded:** the mirroring constant 16 -> 64; the service-gap fixture's wall-clock absolutes 41/20 -> **166/83 ms**; the `kWindowOwnerExpectedRequiredLead`-as-handoff-phase sites now compute `declaredRequiredLeadFor(<their count>)`; the grain-cost sweep's loops 64 -> **128 bars** (and its loop-length-independence pair 64/32 -> 128/48); the two-holder fixtures 200 -> **300 bars**; the increment-24 retention fixtures 30 -> **70 bars** with 100-note windows; the charge fixture 4/20 -> **12/40 bars**; the refusals-by-name fixture 30 -> **70 bars** with 100-note windows — each either a pin re-pointed at the measured declaration or a shape moved *inside* it. Verified: focused **90/90** (zero failures), full native **2,733 / 2,726 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, build **SUCCESS** with the RAM1 line **byte-identical** (`variables 96,192`, code 390,472 + padding 2,744 — constants, accounting and comments only), `git diff --check` clean, `openspec validate --strict` valid; **M127** (per-turn term back to the placeholder bar) fails **19 fixtures**, **M128** (lead judged on the basis counts) and **M129** (denial allowance back to 3) fail their named assertions, all restored byte-identically (`include/Track.h 3ae6b899699f2692`, `src/Track/TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp 1ff579cb96e31498`, `src/Track/TrackPlaybackRuntime.cpp 35eec9683a0fdfd2`, `include/TrackPlaybackRuntime.h 2e50b234a0cce56c`). One device run per tempo, an instrumented build, per-block maxima: the declaration is set from the worst *measured* scheduling maximum with a stated margin, and the next leg can tighten it the same way. **Owed unchanged:** activation (the callers' qualified clock stamps), increment 24's re-attempt, a production requester, the `H x K` sweep. **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 26: the permitted service-gap limit is **wired** into the live lane, and its exceedance is **named** (blocker 3 — half closed).** Step 4 *declared* the limit; this increment makes the **capture lane** compare against it (**corrected below**: a review showed the comparison is compiled out of a non-capture build, so it is telemetry rather than live enforcement): `PlaybackLaneMeasurement` gained `permittedAdvanceTicks`, `overruns` and `overrunMaxTicks`, `observe()` takes the permitted advance (default `0` = *no comparison*, so the clock-plumbing fixtures are untouched), and it counts an overrun **only** for a gap whose predecessor was **eligible** — the eligibility split the sampler already records is exactly what tells a scheduling delay from idle time, which is the separation the increment-25c device legs demanded. The block row is now **schema 3** (`permittedAdvanceTicks, overruns, overrunMaxTicks`) and a **named** row `#CAP,<us>,DIAG,win_gap_overrun,<permitted>,<overruns>,<overrunMaxTicks>,<running>,<epoch>` is emitted once per block that saw one, through the `#ifndef`-guarded seam pattern every other lane row uses. The limit is read **from the declaration** (`kPlaybackViewPermittedAdvancePerTurn`), so the bound and the observation cannot drift. **Why this matters:** the 70-tick blocked gap measured in the increment-25c leg was recorded as a maximum and reported to *nobody*; a gap above the permitted advance across an eligible turn is now an **event in the stream**, carrying the value it was compared against. **Fixture** `test_the_declared_permitted_gap_is_wired_and_its_overrun_is_named` (a gap at the limit is not an overrun and the block carries the limit; one tick past it is counted, sized and named; an **idle** gap above it is *not* an overrun; an **epoch change** is a discontinuity, not an overrun) — including one repair of my own, recorded: the fixture's first version let the **inter-case** gap form its own block, so a case inherited the previous case's overrun. **Mutations M130-M133** (the comparison removed; every gap counted regardless of eligibility; the named row not emitted; the block row no longer carrying the limit) each fail their named assertion and were restored byte-identically (`PlaybackLaneMeasurement.h 3245e37db9c710b7`, `TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp c94103e134533e2a`). Wiring the deadline into it needs three pinned decisions (recorded in the packet): the **episode key** (the lag state keys on `(intervalStart, intervalLength)` while the admitted record retains only `handoffPhase` — so either `admittedIntervalLength` is retained, a measured +8 B per-slot re-base, or the coverage is exposed from the fill state), the **clock reaching the turn** (`stepPlaybackViewMaintenance` takes a phase only; `main.cpp` already holds the clock for sampling), and **what a deadline miss means at completion** (resolve with `replacementReady = false`, name it through the one implementation, never extend `deadlineTick`). **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 27: blocker 3's second half — the admitted deadline is serviced on the live path (and a review's correction of the first half is recorded).** A review of increment 26 (pasted into the session and **independently verified here**) showed that landing claimed too much: the permitted-gap comparison lives inside `#if defined(SESSION_CAPTURE) || defined(PIO_UNIT_TEST_NATIVE)`, so it is **capture-lane telemetry**, not live enforcement — the wording is corrected in this entry and in the `s310u` packet (Addendum 3), and the same review supplied the oracle for the half that was still missing. **Increment 27 lands that half**, adopting the review's six requirements verbatim: the promise the admission makes (`PlaybackViewAdmittedWork::deadlineTick`/`clockEpoch`) is now **read where it is kept** — `Track::serviceAdmittedDeadlineMisses(clock)` runs at the **top of every lane turn for every slot holding a live promise**, so a build that has **not finished** is judged too (R1: independent of completion, the case a completion-time check structurally cannot see); each traversal of the promised interval is counted **exactly once**, computed from the clock and keyed on the promise's own admission tick, with only the traversals that still change the policy accounted (R2); the promise is judged only in the **epoch it was qualified in**, so a reset, seek or re-projection claims nothing and **erases nothing**, and a new promise starts its own count on its own interval (R3); the service only accounts and reports — it publishes nothing, adopts nothing and rebuilds nothing, so the previous revision keeps serving for the missed traversal and a late arrival waits for an eligible boundary (R4); the accounting and the latch are **unconditional code**, with only the row behind the capture seam (R5: enforcement, not telemetry — red-proved natively by gating the accounting behind `SESSION_CAPTURE`); and the judgement is **never routed through `resolvePlaybackLag`**, whose `Current` outcome would otherwise mask a late arrival that happens to carry the wanted revision (R6 — the review's sharpest point). What one miss *means* stays in **one implementation** (`Track::noteMissedTraversalForSlot`: the allowance `one_pass_late`, then the named `lag_breach` plus the latch), which `advancePlaybackLagTraversal` now also calls, so the revision rule and the deadline rule share one notion of a miss and differ only in what they judge; the deadline is **never re-positioned**. The promise retains `admittedIntervalLength` (`handoffPhase` is its start), the turn takes the clock the lane dispatcher already holds, and the size pins were re-based **on measurement** (target 6,792 -> **6,816** B, host 8,744 -> **8,768** B — the interval length, an 8-byte promise key and a 2-byte count; per-slot extern storage, so **no RAM1 re-base**, `variables 96,192` unchanged). **Three fixtures** (unfinished-build miss named once per traversal and never re-granted; epoch revalidation without erasure plus a new promise counting from zero; a late arrival named though the served window already carries the wanted revision) and **M134-M139** red-prove the requirements, all restored byte-identically (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp` pre-mutation **518728238943f77a**); one defect of mine was caught by the fixtures (the accounting loop called the helper twice per newly missed traversal, so the breach appeared at the first miss). Verified: focused **94/94**, full native **2,737 / 2,730 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, build **SUCCESS** with the RAM1 line byte-identical, `git diff --check` clean, `openspec validate --strict` valid. No upload and no device claim: production judges nothing (no production path requests a window, and the lane's production builds carry `clockEpoch == 0`), but the policy now **is** enforcement were a promise admitted. **Blocker 3 verdict:** both halves are in — the limit compared and named in the capture lane, and the admitted deadline serviced, named and latched on the live path independent of capture — while the envelope is still **not** claimed as qualified normal-operation continuity (the blocked gaps the device legs measured are exactly why the policy reports), activation still awaits the callers' qualified clock stamps, and the production requester, the re-attempt (O8) and the `H x K` sweep remain owed. **2026-10-04 — `windowed-playback-generation` slice 3.10, increment 28: a review's three correctness gaps in the deadline service are closed, and containment is proved rather than counted.** A read-only review of increment 27 (pasted into the session and **independently verified here at `5cbd3bb8`**) confirmed three gaps and one unproven claim, all real. **(1) Request deduplication had become fault history.** `serviceAdmittedDeadlineMisses` called `lagState.resetEpisode(...)` whenever `admittedTick` changed, so a repeated request for the **same interval** minted a fresh first-miss allowance — exactly what DEC-108 §13(a) forbids (*"a later edit never resets an earlier interval's missed-deadline allowance"*). Now the per-promise traversal count still starts at zero (that *is* the deduplication) while the **episode** is reset only when the *interval* changes (`coversInterval(handoffPhase, admittedIntervalLength)` guards the call), so the interval's second miss is the named breach instead of another allowance. **(2) An epoch mismatch was skipped, not revalidated.** The service `continue`d silently, and publication had no clock-validity step. §13(c) says a changed clock invalidates the *promise*, never the content, and that the miss **is reported**: the mismatch now names `promise_epoch_invalidated` **once per promise** (per-slot `invalidatedPromiseTick`), claims no traversal miss, leaves the interval's history untouched, and retains the obligation **unmodified** (same admission tick, same deadline) so returning to that clock judges *that* promise again — so an epoch change can never mint an allowance. The content still publishes, which is **asserted**, not assumed. **(3) A deadline crossed at/around the final grain escaped.** The turn's clock is read *before* the worker grain and `activeViewBuildWork()` returns null the moment the build completes, so a build finishing a tick late was never judged. The promise is now **retained through completion** (`completedPromisePendingJudgement`, consumed by the next opportunity's fresh clock, and **cleared by a new admission** so a successor can never be judged as its predecessor). **(4) The review's closing point — *"accounting plus a latch does not yet prove late-publication containment"*** — is now a fixture: after the breach, `containmentForSlot(slot, phase)` reads `ContinuityContainment::ServeLastCoherentRevision` while coverage remains, so the policy is **read by containment**, not merely counted. **Fixtures (3, ownership suite):** the repeated-request + containment fixture (the successor promise's miss is the interval's second — named `lag_breach`, latch set, `one_pass_late` still 1); the real-epoch-change fixture (named once, no traversal count moved, obligation retained and re-judged on the return leg, the build **completes in the new epoch** and publishes, and a promise admitted in that epoch that misses is the **breach**); and the completion fixture (finished *inside* the promise, the record then unreadable, and the next opportunity past the deadline still names `one_pass_late` — once). **MC1-MC6** red-prove each behaviour (always reset the episode; skip the naming; reset on the mismatch; drop the retention gate; drop the retention record; never latch on the second miss) with every restore byte-identical (`TrackPlaybackWindowBuild.cpp` **377b5041b44a8f9d** before and after each case; final **6f4961ef38d9186c** after the doc comments, `TrackPlaybackRuntime.h` **c9b5654c266b5138**). Two corrections were recorded rather than smoothed: the epoch fixture's first draft asserted an absolute `one_pass_late == 0` where its own earlier turn legitimately counted the allowance (now a *no-move* comparison), and the retention is a bool cleared at admission rather than a `tick != 0` sentinel, because tick 0 is a legal instant. Verified: focused **97/97** (94/94 at increment 27), full native **2,740 / 2,733 succeeded / 7 skipped / 0 failed**, build **SUCCESS** with the RAM1 line byte-identical (`variables 96,192`, code 390,472 + padding 2,744) and one measured size re-base (target 6,816 -> **6,832** B, host 8,768 -> **8,784** B), `git diff --check` clean, `openspec validate --strict` valid. No upload and no device claim. **The review's verdict stands where it is about operation:** on the device the service still judges nothing (no production requester, the lane's production builds carry `clockEpoch == 0`, `sInterferenceBudgetEnforced` off), so blocker 3's operational half remains the production requester's qualified clock stamp.
